functions.name: CAuthBase::SetLoginInfo
functions.signature: virtual void CAuthBase::SetLoginInfo(const CString& sUsername, const CString& sPassword, CZNCSock* pSock)
functions.description: Updates the credentials and associated socket for this authentication attempt. Intended to refresh username/password and the socket before completing AcceptLogin/RefuseLogin.
requirements: sUsername: unknown (no explicit constraints documented).
sPassword: unknown (no explicit constraints documented).
pSock may be null or non-null; behavior if null is unspecified in this header.
May be called before AcceptLogin() or RefuseLogin(); no ordering guarantees are documented.

functions.name: CAuthBase::AcceptLogin
functions.description: Marks the authentication attempt as successful for the provided user and triggers subclass handling via AcceptedLogin(). Has no effect after Invalidate().
requirements: User must refer to a valid CUser instance for which authentication succeeded.
If Invalidate() was called, AcceptLogin() will have no effect (as documented).
Side effects and further processing are implemented by subclasses via AcceptedLogin().

functions.name: CAuthBase::RefuseLogin
functions.description: Denies the authentication attempt, optionally providing a reason, and invokes subclass handling via RefusedLogin(). Has no effect after Invalidate().
requirements: sReason: unknown content; may be used for logging or user feedback.
If Invalidate() was called, RefuseLogin() will have no effect (as documented).

functions.name: CAuthBase::GetUsername
functions.description: Returns the username associated with this authentication attempt.

functions.name: CAuthBase::GetPassword
functions.description: Returns the password associated with this authentication attempt.

functions.name: CAuthBase::GetSocket
functions.description: Returns the underlying socket associated with this authentication attempt. The pointer can be null if no socket is set or after Invalidate().

functions.name: CAuthBase::GetRemoteIP
functions.description: Returns the remote IP address of the associated socket. If no socket is set, the return value is unspecified by this header.

functions.name: CAuthBase::Invalidate
functions.description: Invalidates this CAuthBase instance so it no longer uses the socket; subsequent AcceptLogin() or RefuseLogin() calls have no effect.
requirements: After Invalidate(), callers should not expect AcceptLogin()/RefuseLogin() to do anything.

functions.name: CClientAuth::CClientAuth
functions.signature: CClientAuth::CClientAuth(CClient* pClient, const CString& sUsername, const CString& sPassword)
functions.description: Constructs a CClientAuth bound to a specific client with initial username and password to perform client authentication workflow.
requirements: pClient must be a valid pointer to a CClient for which authentication is being performed.
sUsername and sPassword: unknown constraints.

functions.name: CClientAuth::Invalidate
functions.description: Invalidates the authentication object and disassociates it from the client, then calls base CAuthBase::Invalidate().
requirements: After this call, the object will not reference the client and AcceptLogin()/RefuseLogin() on the base will have no effect.

functions.name: CClientAuth::AcceptedLogin
functions.description: Subclass hook invoked when login is accepted. Performs client-specific post-login behavior (details defined in implementation).
requirements: User must be a valid authenticated user.
Caller should not call this directly; use CAuthBase::AcceptLogin().

functions.name: CClientAuth::RefusedLogin
functions.description: Subclass hook invoked when login is refused, performing client-specific handling such as sending notices or cleanup (implementation-defined).
requirements: Caller should not call this directly; use CAuthBase::RefuseLogin().
sReason: free-form explanatory text; no constraints documented.

functions.name: CClient::CClient
functions.description: Constructs a client connection handler (an IRC socket for the user’s client). Initializes capability flags and connection state (details in implementation).

functions.name: CClient::~CClient
functions.description: Destructor for the client connection handler. Cleans up resources and detaches from user/network as needed (implementation-defined).

functions.name: CClient::SendRequiredPasswordNotice
functions.description: Sends a notice to the client indicating that a password is required. Typically used when a connection attempts to proceed without required credentials.

functions.name: CClient::AcceptLogin
functions.description: Accepts login for the provided user and finalizes the client’s authenticated state. May trigger capability negotiation or initial messages.
requirements: User must represent a valid, existing ZNC user that this client is authenticating as.

functions.name: CClient::RefuseLogin
functions.description: Refuses the login attempt for this client with a textual reason and performs necessary cleanup/notification.
requirements: sReason: free-form reason; no explicit constraints.

functions.name: CClient::GetNick
functions.description: Returns the client’s nickname. If bAllowIRCNick is true, may return the IRC nickname from the active IRC socket; otherwise returns a stored/local nickname.

functions.name: CClient::GetNickMask
functions.description: Returns a nick!user@host style mask for this client, if available. Details depend on current connection state and implementation.

functions.name: CClient::GetIdentifier
functions.description: Returns the identifier string for this client (client id parsed from credentials, if any).

functions.name: CClient::CapVersion
functions.description: Returns the negotiated IRCv3 capability protocol version (e.g., 302).

functions.name: CClient::HasCap302
functions.description: Returns true if the client’s negotiated capability version is 302 or newer.

functions.name: CClient::HasCapNotify
functions.description: Returns true if the client requested and has cap-notify capability enabled.

functions.name: CClient::HasAwayNotify
functions.description: Returns true if the client requested and has away-notify capability enabled.

functions.name: CClient::HasAccountNotify
functions.description: Returns true if the client requested and has account-notify capability enabled.

functions.name: CClient::HasInviteNotify
functions.description: Returns true if the client requested and has invite-notify capability enabled.

functions.name: CClient::HasExtendedJoin
functions.description: Returns true if the client requested and has extended-join capability enabled.

functions.name: CClient::HasNamesx
functions.description: Returns true if the client requested and has namesx capability enabled.

functions.name: CClient::HasUHNames
functions.description: Returns true if the client requested and has userhost-in-names (uhnames) capability enabled.

functions.name: CClient::HasChgHost
functions.description: Returns true if the client requested and has chghost capability enabled.

functions.name: CClient::IsAway
functions.description: Returns true if the client is currently marked away.

functions.name: CClient::HasServerTime
functions.description: Returns true if the client requested and has server-time capability enabled.

functions.name: CClient::HasBatch
functions.description: Returns true if the client requested and has batch capability enabled.

functions.name: CClient::HasEchoMessage
functions.description: Returns true if the client requested and has echo-message capability enabled.

functions.name: CClient::HasSelfMessage
functions.description: Returns true if the client requested and has self-message capability enabled.

functions.name: CClient::IsValidIdentifier
functions.description: Returns whether the provided client identifier string is valid according to ZNC’s identifier rules. Actual validation rules are defined in the implementation.
requirements: sIdentifier: unknown constraints beyond being a CString; exact allowed characters/length are not documented here.

functions.name: CClient::UserCommand
functions.description: Parses and executes a ZNC user command received from the client. The input line may be modified during processing.
requirements: sLine should contain a single user command in text form; exact syntax is implementation-specific.
The caller passes a non-const reference to allow in-place modifications.

functions.name: CClient::UserPortCommand
functions.description: Parses and executes a user command received via a dedicated user port. The input may be modified during processing.
requirements: sLine should contain a single command targeted at the user port; exact syntax is implementation-specific.

functions.name: CClient::StatusCTCP
functions.description: Handles a STATUS CTCP command directed at ZNC’s status context.
requirements: sCommand: the CTCP command payload; specific accepted values are implementation-defined.

functions.name: CClient::BouncedOff
functions.description: Handles the case where a client connection is bounced off (e.g., detached or refused). Performs any necessary notifications/cleanup.

functions.name: CClient::IsAttached
functions.description: Returns true if this client is currently attached to a user (m_pUser is non-null).

functions.name: CClient::IsPlaybackActive
functions.description: Returns whether playback mode is currently active for this client.

functions.name: CClient::SetPlaybackActive
functions.description: Enables or disables playback mode for this client.

functions.name: CClient::PutIRC
functions.description: Sends a raw line to the upstream IRC server on behalf of the client.
requirements: sLine: should represent a valid IRC protocol line; exact formatting constraints are not specified in this header.

functions.name: CClient::PutIRCStripping
functions.description: Sends a message to the server after stripping any prefix and possibly tags. Used to sanitize a message before relaying it upstream.
requirements: Message should be a well-formed CMessage; unsupported elements will be stripped. Exact stripping rules are implementation-defined.

functions.name: CClient::PutClientRaw
functions.description: Sends a raw data line to the client without capability/tag filtering. The unmodified line is first offered to the CModule::OnSendToClient() hook; if not halted, it is sent to the client. Prefer PutClient() when possible.
requirements: Be aware that bypassing message/tag filtering may confuse older IRC clients (as warned in comments).
sLine: unknown constraints; should be a single protocol line. The function returns false only if a module halts or sending fails (exact conditions not detailed).

functions.name: CClient::PutClient
functions.description: Sends a text line to the client after applying compatibility filtering performed by the CMessage-based overload internally (details implementation-specific).
requirements: Prefer using the CMessage overload to benefit from capability/tag filtering when constructing structured IRC messages.

functions.name: CClient::PutClient
functions.description: Sends a message to the client, ensuring only messages and tags that the client has explicitly requested are sent. This enforces compatibility with various IRC clients. Returns true if the message was sent, false if it was ignored.
requirements: Message should be a well-formed CMessage.

Some message types require specific capabilities to be enabled by the client: ACCOUNT requires account-notify; AWAY requires away-notify; INVITE for others requires invite-notify; TAGMSG requires message-tags.
Supported tags include: time (requires server-time), batch (requires batch), any tag requires message-tags unless registered via SetTagSupport().
Bypassing this filtering by using PutClientRaw(Message.ToString()) may cause issues with older clients (documented warning).

functions.name: CClient::PutStatus
functions.description: Sends a formatted status table to the client’s status window and returns the number of lines sent.
requirements: table: must be a valid CTable with desired rows/columns; exact formatting is implementation-defined.

functions.name: CClient::PutStatus
functions.description: Sends a single status line to the client’s status window.
requirements: sLine: free-form text.

functions.name: CClient::PutStatusNotice
functions.description: Sends a status notice line to the client’s status window.
requirements: sLine: free-form text.

functions.name: CClient::PutModule
functions.signature: void CClient::PutModule(const CString& sModule, const CString& sLine)
functions.description: Sends a message line from a specific module to the client, typically prefixed/namespaced by module name.
requirements: sModule: name of the module emitting the message.
sLine: message text.

functions.name: CClient::PutModNotice
functions.signature: void CClient::PutModNotice(const CString& sModule, const CString& sLine)
functions.description: Sends a notice from a specific module to the client’s status or module context.
requirements: sModule: module name.
sLine: notice text.

functions.name: CClient::IsCapEnabled
functions.description: Returns true if the named capability is currently enabled (accepted) for this client.
requirements: sCap: capability name string (e.g., "server-time").

functions.name: CClient::IsTagEnabled
functions.description: Returns true if the named IRCv3 message tag is registered as supported by this client.
requirements: sTag: tag name without leading '+', '@', or vendor namespace qualifiers, as used internally. Exact form is implementation-defined.

functions.name: CClient::SetTagSupport
functions.signature: void CClient::SetTagSupport(const CString& sTag, bool bState)
functions.description: Registers a message tag as supported or unsupported by the client. This affects which tags ZNC will send to the client (does not affect tags sent by the client).
requirements: sTag: tag name to update.
bState: true to mark as supported; false to mark as unsupported.

functions.name: CClient::NotifyServerDependentCap
functions.signature: void CClient::NotifyServerDependentCap(const CString& sCap, bool bValue, const CString& sValue)
functions.description: Notifies the client about a single capability that depends on the upstream IRC server’s support, indicating enable/disable and an optional value.
requirements: sCap: capability name.
bValue: true to indicate enabled/available, false otherwise.
sValue: optional capability value; semantics are cap-specific.

functions.name: CClient::ReadLine
functions.description: Handles an incoming raw line from the connected client, parses it into IRC messages/commands, and routes accordingly.
requirements: sData should be a single received line from the client; exact format handling is implementation-defined.

functions.name: CClient::SendMotd
functions.description: Sends the Message of the Day (MOTD) to the client. Returns true on success, false otherwise.

functions.name: CClient::HelpUser
functions.description: Sends help text to the client, optionally filtered by a substring or topic string.
requirements: sFilter: optional filter; empty string shows general help.

functions.name: CClient::AuthUser
functions.description: Begins or continues the process of authenticating this client connection (e.g., handling PASS/USER/NICK or capability-based auth).

functions.name: CClient::Connected
functions.description: Socket callback invoked when the client connection is established. Performs initialization such as greeting or capability negotiation.

functions.name: CClient::Timeout
functions.description: Socket callback invoked when the connection times out. Performs timeout handling and cleanup.

functions.name: CClient::Disconnected
functions.description: Socket callback invoked when the client disconnects. Performs cleanup and detachment.

functions.name: CClient::ConnectionRefused
functions.description: Socket callback invoked when a connection attempt is refused. Handles error reporting and cleanup.

functions.name: CClient::ReachedMaxBuffer
functions.description: Socket callback invoked when the send buffer limit is reached. Triggers backpressure handling or disconnect logic.

functions.name: CClient::SetNick
functions.description: Sets the stored nickname for this client context.
requirements: s: nickname string; no constraints are documented here.

functions.name: CClient::SetAway
functions.description: Marks the client as away or back.
requirements: bAway: true to mark away; false to mark back.

functions.name: CClient::GetUser
functions.description: Returns the currently attached user pointer, or nullptr if unattached.

functions.name: CClient::SetNetwork
functions.signature: void CClient::SetNetwork(CIRCNetwork* pNetwork, bool bDisconnect = true, bool bReconnect = true)
functions.description: Attaches this client to the specified IRC network, optionally disconnecting from the current one and reconnecting. Manages client-to-network association.
requirements: pNetwork: pointer to a CIRCNetwork; must be valid. Ownership/lifetime requirements are not described here.
bDisconnect: if true, the current network connection may be disconnected (implementation-defined).
bReconnect: if true, may trigger reconnection to the new network (implementation-defined).

functions.name: CClient::GetNetwork
functions.description: Returns the currently associated IRC network, or nullptr if none.

functions.name: CClient::GetClients
functions.description: Returns a vector reference of client connections relevant to this context (e.g., all clients attached to the same user/network). Exact contents are implementation-defined.
requirements: Returned reference remains valid as long as the owning object maintains it; do not store beyond its lifetime.

functions.name: CClient::GetIRCSock
functions.description: Returns a const pointer to the upstream IRC socket associated with the current network, or nullptr if not connected.

functions.name: CClient::GetIRCSock
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the upstream IRC socket associated with the current network, or nullptr if not connected.

functions.name: CClient::GetFullName
functions.description: Returns the full name/gecos string for this client, if known.

functions.name: CClient::SendSASLChallenge
functions.description: Sends an AUTHENTICATE message to the client during SASL, encoding the payload as Base64 and splitting across multiple IRC messages if needed.
requirements: sMessage: raw challenge/response chunk before Base64 encoding.

functions.name: CClient::RefuseSASLLogin
functions.description: Sends SASL failure numerics to the client and terminates the SASL login attempt with the provided reason.
requirements: sReason: explanatory text; no constraints documented.

functions.name: CClient::AcceptSASLLogin
functions.description: Completes a successful SASL login for the given user, sending success numerics and marking the user as authenticated for this client.
requirements: User must be a valid user matching the SASL credentials.

functions.name: CClient::StartSASLPasswordCheck
functions.signature: void CClient::StartSASLPasswordCheck(const CString& sUser, const CString& sPassword, const CString& sAuthorizationId)
functions.description: Starts a (potentially asynchronous) verification of SASL credentials, typically for SASL PLAIN. On completion, sends success/failure SASL numerics. The authorization id is parsed via ParseUser() to extract network and client id.
requirements: sUser should match the username from sAuthorizationId either fully or just the username part (as documented).
sPassword: the password to verify; no format constraints documented.
sAuthorizationId: may include username, client id, and network; will be parsed by ParseUser().

functions.name: CClient::ParseUser
functions.description: Parses an authorization line to gather username, client id, and network name (if present), and returns the username cleaned of those components.
requirements: sAuthLine: an auth string possibly containing username, client id, and network. Exact syntax is implementation-defined.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::IsValidNetwork
functions.description: Returns whether the provided network name string is valid for use with CIRCNetwork. Typical use is to validate user-supplied network identifiers before creating/renaming a network. Specific validation rules are not documented here.
requirements: sNetwork should be a non-empty string.
Exact character/length restrictions are unknown (not documented in this header).

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::CIRCNetwork
functions.description: Constructs a new IRC network object bound to a user with the given network name. Use this to create a network configuration/state for a user.
requirements: pUser must point to a valid CUser instance and remain valid for the lifetime of the CIRCNetwork.
sName should pass IsValidNetwork() (exact rules not documented).

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::~CIRCNetwork
functions.description: Destructor for the IRC network object. Cleans up network-related resources owned by this instance.
requirements: The CIRCNetwork instance must not be used after destruction.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::Clone
functions.signature: void CIRCNetwork::Clone(const CIRCNetwork& Network, bool bCloneName = true);
functions.description: Copies configuration/state from another CIRCNetwork into this instance. Optionally clones the source network’s name.
requirements: &Network must refer to a valid CIRCNetwork.
If bCloneName is true, GetName() may change; callers relying on the previous name should update their references.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::GetNetworkPath
functions.description: Returns the filesystem path associated with this network (e.g., for storing per-network data). Exact format is implementation-specific.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::DelServers
functions.description: Removes all configured IRC servers from this network.
requirements: After calling, GetServers() becomes empty; any iterators/pointers to previously stored CServer objects become invalid.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::ParseConfig
functions.signature: bool CIRCNetwork::ParseConfig(CConfig* pConfig, CString& sError, bool bUpgrade = false);
functions.description: Parses and applies configuration for this network from the provided CConfig. On failure, writes an error message to sError. Optionally upgrades legacy formats if bUpgrade is true.
requirements: pConfig must point to a valid CConfig object containing network-related configuration.
sError is used as an output parameter and will be modified on failure.
If bUpgrade is true, caller should be prepared for configuration changes.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::ToConfig
functions.description: Serializes this network’s configuration to a CConfig object for persistence or inspection.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::BounceAllClients
functions.description: Disconnects and (typically) reconnects all IRC clients attached to this network, e.g., after network-level settings change. Exact behavior is implementation-defined.
requirements: There must be clients attached for any visible effect.
Clients may observe disconnects/reconnects; callers should ensure this is acceptable.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::IsUserAttached
functions.description: Returns true if at least one client is currently attached to this network.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::IsUserOnline
functions.description: Returns true if the user is considered online for this network (e.g., has active client connections). Exact condition is implementation-defined.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::ClientConnected
functions.description: Registers a client as connected to this network. Typically called when a user’s frontend connection attaches.
requirements: pClient must be a valid, initialized CClient pointer.
pClient should not already be registered as connected to this network.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::ClientDisconnected
functions.description: Registers that a previously connected client has disconnected from this network.
requirements: pClient must be a valid, initialized CClient pointer that was previously connected via ClientConnected().

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::GetUser
functions.description: Returns the CUser associated with this network.
requirements: Returned pointer may be null if the network has no user set (not specified). Caller should check for null.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::GetName
functions.description: Returns this network’s name.
requirements: Returned reference remains valid while the CIRCNetwork exists and the name is not changed.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::IsNetworkAttached
functions.description: Alias of IsUserAttached(): returns true if at least one client is attached to this network.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::GetClients
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the list of clients attached to this network.
requirements: Do not store references/iterators across mutations to the client list.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::FindClients
functions.description: Returns a list of clients that match the provided identifier (matching criteria implementation-defined, e.g., by name/label).
requirements: sIdentifier should be a non-empty string for meaningful results.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::SetUser
functions.description: Associates this network with the given user object.
requirements: pUser must be a valid CUser pointer and should outlive or match the lifecycle expectations of this CIRCNetwork.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::SetName
functions.description: Attempts to set/rename this network’s name.
requirements: sName should pass IsValidNetwork() (exact rules not documented).
May fail and return false if the name is invalid or conflicts (implementation-defined).

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::GetModules
functions.description: Returns a modifiable reference to the module manager for this network.
requirements: Returned reference must not be used after the CIRCNetwork is destroyed.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::PutUser
functions.signature: bool CIRCNetwork::PutUser(const CString& sLine, CClient* pClient = nullptr, CClient* pSkipClient = nullptr);
functions.description: Sends a line of text to one or more attached clients for this network. Optionally target a specific client and/or skip a specific client.
requirements: sLine should be a single message line; content format is implementation/IRC-protocol dependent (not specified here).
pClient, if non-null, must point to a connected client attached to this network.
pSkipClient, if non-null, must point to a connected client attached to this network.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::PutStatus
functions.signature: bool CIRCNetwork::PutStatus(const CString& sLine, CClient* pClient = nullptr, CClient* pSkipClient = nullptr);
functions.description: Sends a status message line to attached clients (e.g., to a status window), optionally targeting or skipping a specific client.
requirements: sLine should be a single message line; exact format is implementation-defined.
pClient/pSkipClient, if provided, must be clients attached to this network.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::PutModule
functions.signature: bool CIRCNetwork::PutModule(const CString& sModule, const CString& sLine, CClient* pClient = nullptr, CClient* pSkipClient = nullptr);
functions.description: Sends a message from/for a specific module to attached clients, optionally targeting or skipping a particular client.
requirements: sModule should be a non-empty module identifier.
sLine should be a single message line; exact format is implementation-defined.
pClient/pSkipClient, if provided, must be clients attached to this network.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::GetChans
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the list of channels tracked by this network.
requirements: Do not store references/iterators across mutations to the channel list.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::FindChan
functions.description: Finds and returns a channel by name (case/normalization rules implementation-defined).
requirements: sName should be a valid channel name for this network.
Returned pointer may be null if not found; caller must check for null.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::FindChans
functions.description: Returns channels whose names match the given wildcard/pattern. Matching semantics are implementation-defined.
requirements: sWild should be a non-empty pattern for meaningful results.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::AddChan
functions.description: Adds an existing channel object to this network’s channel list.
requirements: pChan must point to a valid CChan not already owned/managed by another network here.
Ownership/lifetime becomes managed by this network (exact ownership semantics not specified).

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::DelChan
functions.description: Removes a channel by name from this network’s channel list.
requirements: sName should match an existing channel name.
After deletion, any pointers/iterators to the channel become invalid.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::MoveChan
functions.signature: bool CIRCNetwork::MoveChan(const CString& sChan, unsigned int index, CString& sError);
functions.description: Reorders a channel to the given index within the channel list. On failure, writes a reason to sError.
requirements: sChan must name an existing channel.
index must be within the valid range [0, number_of_channels] (exact bounds handling unspecified).
sError is an output parameter and may be modified on failure.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::SwapChans
functions.signature: bool CIRCNetwork::SwapChans(const CString& sChan1, const CString& sChan2, CString& sError);
functions.description: Swaps the positions of two channels in the channel list. On failure, writes a reason to sError.
requirements: sChan1 and sChan2 must refer to existing channels within this network.
sError is an output parameter and may be modified on failure.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::JoinChans
functions.description: Attempts to join all channels configured on this network (subject to delays, connection state, etc.).
requirements: Typically requires an active IRC connection for effect (not enforced by signature).

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::GetQueries
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the list of private message queries tracked by this network.
requirements: Do not store references/iterators across mutations to the query list.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::FindQuery
functions.description: Finds and returns a query by peer name/nick. Returns null if not found.
requirements: sName should be a non-empty nick/identifier.
Caller must check for null.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::FindQueries
functions.description: Returns queries whose peer names match the provided wildcard/pattern. Matching semantics are implementation-defined.
requirements: sWild should be a non-empty pattern for meaningful results.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::AddQuery
functions.description: Creates and adds a query (private conversation) with the given peer name and returns it.
requirements: sName should be a valid peer/nick identifier.
Returned pointer may be null on failure (not specified); caller should check results.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::DelQuery
functions.description: Deletes a query by peer name from this network.
requirements: sName should match an existing query.
After deletion, any pointers to the removed CQuery become invalid.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::GetChanPrefixes
functions.description: Returns the set of valid channel prefix characters for this network (e.g., # & + !).

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::SetChanPrefixes
functions.description: Sets the valid channel prefix characters for this network.
requirements: s should contain only valid prefix characters for the IRC server; exact validation unspecified.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::IsChan
functions.description: Returns true if sChan looks like a channel name on this network, based on configured prefixes.
requirements: sChan should be a non-empty string.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::GetServers
functions.description: Returns the list of configured IRC servers for this network.
requirements: Do not store references/iterators across mutations to the server list.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::HasServers
functions.description: Returns true if at least one IRC server is configured for this network.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::FindServer
functions.description: Finds a configured server by name/host. Returns null if not found.
requirements: sName should be a non-empty hostname or identifier.
Caller must check for null.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::DelServer
functions.signature: bool CIRCNetwork::DelServer(const CString& sName, unsigned short uPort, const CString& sPass);
functions.description: Removes a configured server matching the given host, port, and password.
requirements: sName should match an existing server’s host/identifier.
uPort should be within valid TCP port range (0–65535; typical usable 1–65535).
sPass must match the stored server password, if any.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::AddServer
functions.description: Adds the provided server object to the configured server list.
requirements: Server should be fully initialized with at least host and port.
May fail if a duplicate already exists (implementation-defined).

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::GetNextServer
functions.description: Returns the next server to try, optionally advancing the internal server index.
requirements: If bAdvance is true, the internal current-server pointer is advanced and may wrap; callers should handle null if no servers exist.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::GetCurrentServer
functions.description: Returns the currently selected/active server, or null if none.
requirements: Caller must handle a null return if there is no current server.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::SetIRCServer
functions.description: Sets a textual IRC server spec for this network (e.g., for display or parsing).
requirements: s should be a non-empty server specification string.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::SetNextServer
functions.description: Sets the next server to use to the specified configured server.
requirements: pServer must point to a server object that exists within this network’s configured server list.
Returns false if the server is not found in this network.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::IsLastServer
functions.description: Returns true if the current server index points at the last server in the rotation/list.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::GetTrustedFingerprints
functions.description: Returns the set of trusted TLS certificate fingerprints configured for this network.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::AddTrustedFingerprint
functions.description: Adds a fingerprint to the trusted set for TLS connections. The string is stored escaped/normalized for hex with colons.
requirements: sFP should be a valid fingerprint string; it will be normalized via Escape_n(EHEXCOLON).

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::DelTrustedFingerprint
functions.description: Removes a fingerprint from the trusted set.
requirements: sFP should match the stored representation of the fingerprint.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::ClearTrustedFingerprints
functions.description: Clears all trusted TLS certificate fingerprints for this network.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::SetIRCConnectEnabled
functions.description: Enables or disables the network’s ability to connect to IRC servers.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::GetIRCConnectEnabled
functions.description: Returns whether IRC connection attempts are enabled for this network.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::GetIRCSock
functions.description: Returns the IRC socket object for this network, or null if disconnected/not created.
requirements: Caller must handle a null return.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::GetIRCServer
functions.description: Returns the textual IRC server specification for this network.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::GetIRCNick
functions.description: Returns the current IRC nick state object associated with this network.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::SetIRCNick
functions.description: Sets the current IRC nick state object for this network.
requirements: n should be a valid CNick instance describing the desired nick.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::GetCurNick
functions.description: Returns the current effective nickname as a string (derived from GetIRCNick or configured nick).

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::IsIRCAway
functions.description: Returns whether the user is marked away on the IRC server for this network.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::SetIRCAway
functions.description: Sets the away status flag for this network.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::Connect
functions.description: Initiates a connection from this network to an IRC server using the configured server list/settings.
requirements: GetIRCConnectEnabled() should be true for connection attempts to proceed.
Requires at least one configured server (HasServers()).
Returns false on immediate failure to initiate; further errors may occur asynchronously.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::IsIRCConnected
functions.description: Returns whether the network is currently connected and authenticated to an IRC server.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::SetIRCSocket
functions.description: Associates the underlying IRC socket with this network (typically called by connection code).
requirements: pIRCSock may be null to clear; if non-null, it must be a valid CIRCSock for this network.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::IRCConnected
functions.description: Notifies the network object that the IRC connection is established (post-registration). Triggers post-connect logic.
requirements: Should be called only once per connection lifecycle at the appropriate time.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::IRCDisconnected
functions.description: Notifies the network object that the IRC connection has been lost/closed. Triggers cleanup/reconnect logic.
requirements: Should be called when the IRC socket disconnects or is closed.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::CheckIRCConnect

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::IsServerCapAccepted

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::PutIRC

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::UpdateMotdBuffer

functions.description: Updates a MOTD buffer entry matched by command to the provided CMessage and optional text.
requirements: sCommand should identify the buffer entry; matching rules are implementation-defined.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::SetAltNick

requirements: s should be a valid IRC nickname; exact validation unspecified.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::SetIdent

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::SetRealName
functions.description: Sets the real name (gecos) for this network.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::SetBindHost

requirements: s should be a valid local interface/hostname; exact validation unspecified.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::SetEncoding
functions.description: Sets the character encoding for this network.
requirements: s should be a valid encoding name recognized by ZNC/build; exact accepted values unspecified.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::SetQuitMsg
functions.description: Sets the quit message for this network.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::GetFloodRate
functions.description: Returns the configured flood rate (messages per second or similar). A value of -1 disables protection (per comment).

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::GetFloodBurst
functions.description: Returns the configured flood burst (number of messages allowed in a burst).

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::SetFloodRate
functions.description: Sets the flood rate. Per comment, set to -1 to disable flood protection.
requirements: fFloodRate should be non-negative or -1 to disable, per the inline member comment.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::SetFloodBurst
functions.description: Sets the flood burst value (how many messages can be sent quickly before rate limiting applies).
requirements: uFloodBurst should be a reasonable non-negative value; exact limits not specified.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::GetJoinDelay

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::SetJoinDelay

requirements: uJoinDelay should be a non-negative value; exact limits not specified.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::SetTrustAllCerts
functions.description: Sets whether to trust all TLS certificates for this network (disables certificate validation when true).
requirements: Use with caution; may reduce security.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::GetTrustAllCerts

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::SetTrustPKI
functions.description: Sets whether to trust the system/public key infrastructure (CA validation) for TLS connections.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::GetTrustPKI

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::BytesRead

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::BytesWritten

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::AddBytesRead
functions.description: Increments the total bytes-read counter by u.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::AddBytesWritten
functions.description: Increments the total bytes-written counter by u.

functions.name: CIRCNetwork::ExpandString
functions.description: Expands variables/placeholders in sStr using network/user context and returns the expanded string.

functions.name: CIRCSock::CIRCSock
functions.description: Constructor for the IRC socket/connection object bound to a specific IRC network context. Initializes per-connection state and prepares the socket to participate in the IRC login/negotiation lifecycle via CIRCSocket callbacks.
requirements: pNetwork must point to a valid CIRCNetwork instance for the lifetime of the CIRCSock object.
Must not be copied; copy constructor is deleted (use a pointer/reference or create a new instance).

functions.name: CIRCSock::~CIRCSock
functions.description: Destructor for the IRC socket/connection. Cleans up any resources associated with the connection state.
requirements: Do not use the object after destruction.
All outstanding operations on the underlying socket should be considered canceled upon destruction.

functions.name: CIRCSock::ReadLine
functions.description: Processes a single raw line of data received from the IRC server. This is an override from CIRCSocket, typically parsing the line into messages and dispatching handlers.
requirements: sData should contain exactly one IRC protocol line without CRLF terminators (inferred from IRC conventions).
Caller should invoke this only with data received from the server; outgoing data must use PutIRC/PutIRCRaw.

functions.name: CIRCSock::Connected
functions.description: Notification callback that the underlying connection has been established. Starts the IRC registration/CAP negotiation sequence.
requirements: Called by the socket framework; user code should not call directly.
May be followed by CAP negotiation and login messages; ensure network configuration (e.g., nick/pass) is set before connection.

functions.name: CIRCSock::Disconnected
functions.description: Notification callback that the underlying connection has closed. Performs cleanup of IRC state.
requirements: Called by the socket framework; user code should not call directly.

functions.name: CIRCSock::ConnectionRefused
functions.description: Callback for a refused connection attempt. Allows the client to react to refusal (e.g., retry/backoff).
requirements: Called by the socket framework; user code should not call directly.

functions.name: CIRCSock::SockError
functions.signature: void CIRCSock::SockError(int iErrno, const CString& sDescription)
functions.description: Callback indicating a socket-level error has occurred, with the OS error code and a description string.
requirements: iErrno should be the system error code associated with the failure.
sDescription should describe the error; may be empty if not available.
Called by the socket framework; user code should not call directly.

functions.name: CIRCSock::Timeout
functions.description: Callback indicating the connection attempt or operation has timed out.
requirements: Called by the socket framework; user code should not call directly.

functions.name: CIRCSock::ReachedMaxBuffer
functions.description: Callback indicating the socket’s maximum buffer has been reached, typically triggering backpressure or disconnect.
requirements: Called by the socket framework; user code should not call directly.

functions.name: CIRCSock::SSLCertError
functions.description: SSL/TLS certificate error callback (only when built with SSL support). Provides the peer certificate for inspection/logging when verification fails.
requirements: Only available when compiled with HAVE_LIBSSL defined.
pCert should point to the peer certificate involved in the verification error; may be null depending on the failure mode (unknown).
Called by the socket framework during SSL handshake; user code should not call directly.

functions.name: CIRCSock::PutIRCRaw
functions.description: Sends a raw IRC line to the server. The line is first passed unmodified to the CModule::OnSendToIRC() hook; if not halted, it is sent as-is. Prefer PutIRC().
requirements: sLine should be a single IRC protocol line without trailing CRLF (inferred from IRC line-based protocol).
Caller is responsible for sending only server-compatible raw lines; bypasses message/tag capability filtering as noted.
May be blocked/modified by module hooks; caller should not assume immediate delivery.

functions.name: CIRCSock::PutIRC
functions.description: Sends a message to the server given as a raw string. See PutIRC(const CMessage&) for details regarding filtering and flood control.
requirements: sLine should represent a valid IRC command line (without CRLF, inferred).
Subject to flood protection and module hooks similarly to PutIRCRaw/PutIRC(const CMessage&).

functions.name: CIRCSock::PutIRCQuick
functions.description: Sends a line to the server with minimal/zero queuing, intended for time-critical responses like PONG.
requirements: Intended only for PONG (as documented); avoid using for general traffic to prevent bypassing flood protection.
sLine should be a valid IRC line without CRLF (inferred).

functions.name: CIRCSock::ResetChans
functions.description: Resets internal channel state for this connection/network, typically clearing known channel lists and modes.
requirements: Should be called when reinitializing network/channel state (e.g., reconnect).
Existing channel pointers/listeners may become invalid after reset (inferred).

functions.name: CIRCSock::Quit
functions.description: Sends a QUIT command to the server, optionally with a quit message, and initiates connection closure.
requirements: sQuitMsg should be an IRC-safe string; server-side length limits may apply (inferred).
After calling, the connection will terminate; callers should be prepared for Disconnected() callback.

functions.name: CIRCSock::PauseCap
functions.description: Pauses sending further CAP requests and CAP END during capability negotiation (e.g., from CModule::OnServerCapResult). Each PauseCap must be paired with a ResumeCap.
requirements: Each call to PauseCap must later be balanced with a matching call to ResumeCap.
Use only during CAP negotiation phases.

functions.name: CIRCSock::ResumeCap
functions.description: Resumes CAP negotiation and login after one or more PauseCap calls. Sends pending CAP requests and/or CAP END as appropriate.
requirements: Must be called once for each prior PauseCap to fully resume CAP flow.
Call only after paused operations (e.g., asynchronous module checks) are complete.

functions.name: CIRCSock::IsTagEnabled
functions.description: Returns whether a message tag is enabled/allowed to be sent to the server according to negotiated capabilities and SetTagSupport.
requirements: sTag should be the exact tag key to test (case and vendor prefix as negotiated).

functions.name: CIRCSock::SetTagSupport
functions.signature: void CIRCSock::SetTagSupport(const CString& sTag, bool bState)
functions.description: Registers local support state for a specific message tag, controlling whether the client may send that tag (does not affect tags received from the server).
requirements: sTag must identify the tag to modify; should be non-empty (inferred).
bState=true to enable, false to disable.

functions.name: CIRCSock::SetPass
functions.description: Sets the password to use for server login (PASS or SASL-related depending on configuration).
requirements: s contains the password; treat as sensitive.
Call before connection or authentication begins to ensure it is used.

functions.name: CIRCSock::GetMaxNickLen
functions.description: Returns the server-advertised maximum nickname length.

functions.name: CIRCSock::GetModeType
functions.description: Returns the argument requirement classification (ListArg/HasArg/ArgWhenSet/NoArg) for a given channel mode character, based on RPL_ISUPPORT (CHANMODE/005).
requirements: cMode should be a valid channel mode character as advertised by the server; unknown modes may return a default classification depending on internal mapping (unknown exact behavior).

functions.name: CIRCSock::GetPermFromMode
functions.description: Maps a channel mode (e.g., o/v) to its corresponding user permission prefix (e.g., @/+).
requirements: cMode should be a valid user-status channel mode; unknown mappings may return '\0' (unknown exact behavior).

functions.name: CIRCSock::GetModeFromPerm
functions.description: Maps a user permission prefix (e.g., @/+) to its corresponding mode character (e.g., o/v).
requirements: cPerm should be a valid user permission prefix; unknown mappings may return '\0' (unknown exact behavior).

functions.name: CIRCSock::GetChanModes
functions.description: Returns the mapping of channel mode characters to their argument requirement classification as known for the current server.

functions.name: CIRCSock::IsPermChar
functions.description: Returns true if the supplied character is recognized as a user permission prefix (and not '\0').
requirements: c must not be '\0' to be considered; function returns false otherwise.

functions.name: CIRCSock::IsPermMode
functions.description: Returns true if the supplied character is recognized as a user permission mode character (and not '\0').
requirements: c must not be '\0' to be considered; function returns false otherwise.

functions.name: CIRCSock::GetPerms
functions.description: Returns the string of known user permission prefixes (e.g., "@%+") for the server.

functions.name: CIRCSock::GetPermModes
functions.description: Returns the string of user permission mode characters corresponding to the prefixes (e.g., "ov").

functions.name: CIRCSock::GetNickMask
functions.description: Returns the full nick!user@host mask for the current connection nickname.
requirements: Underlying CNick state must be initialized with user/host info to get a complete mask (inferred).

functions.name: CIRCSock::GetNick
functions.description: Returns the current nickname string for this connection.

functions.name: CIRCSock::GetPass
functions.description: Returns the configured server password for this connection.
requirements: Treat the returned reference as sensitive; avoid logging.

functions.name: CIRCSock::GetNetwork
functions.description: Returns the CIRCNetwork this socket belongs to.
requirements: Returned pointer may be null only if not initialized (unknown); typically valid for the object's lifetime.

functions.name: CIRCSock::HasNamesx
functions.description: Returns whether the server supports the NAMESX extension (multi-prefix in NAMES).

functions.name: CIRCSock::HasUHNames
functions.description: Returns whether the server supports userhost-in-NAMES (UHNames).

functions.name: CIRCSock::HasAwayNotify
functions.description: Returns whether the server supports AWAY-notify capability.

functions.name: CIRCSock::HasAccountNotify
functions.description: Returns whether the server supports account-notify capability.

functions.name: CIRCSock::HasExtendedJoin
functions.description: Returns whether the server supports extended-join capability.

functions.name: CIRCSock::HasServerTime
functions.description: Returns whether the server supports the server-time capability.

functions.name: CIRCSock::HasMessageTagCap
functions.description: Returns whether the server negotiated the message tags capability.

functions.name: CIRCSock::GetUserModes
functions.description: Returns the set of user mode characters currently applied to the user on the server (umodes).

functions.name: CIRCSock::IsAuthed
functions.description: Returns true if the connection has successfully passed server welcome (post-001), i.e., is authenticated/registered.

functions.name: CIRCSock::GetAcceptedCaps
functions.description: Returns the set of IRCv3 capabilities (CAP) accepted by the server for this session.

functions.name: CIRCSock::IsCapAccepted
functions.description: Returns true if the specified capability is in the accepted CAP set for this session.
requirements: sCap should be the exact capability token (case per server semantics).

functions.name: CIRCSock::GetCapLsValue
functions.signature: CString CIRCSock::GetCapLsValue(const CString& sKey, const CString& sDefault = "") const
functions.description: Returns the value associated with a capability key from CAP LS, or sDefault if not present.
requirements: sKey should be a capability token key exactly as advertised by the server.

functions.name: CIRCSock::GetISupport
functions.description: Returns the full map of RPL_ISUPPORT tokens (005) to their values for the current server.

functions.name: CIRCSock::IsFloodProtected
functions.description: Returns whether the given sending rate (messages per time unit) should be considered flood-protected according to ZNC’s policy. Useful for determining throttling settings.
requirements: fRate should be a positive rate value (inferred).

functions.name: CIRCSock::IsNickVisibleInAttachedChannels
functions.description: Checks whether the specified nick is currently visible in any channels attached to the user/clients for this network (e.g., for echo/visibility logic).
requirements: sNick should be a valid nickname string per server rules (inferred).
Requires the network/channel state to be populated (e.g., after joins) to return meaningful results (inferred).

functions.name: CZNCSock::CZNCSock
functions.description: Constructor for a ZNC-specific Csock wrapper with an optional socket timeout. Used to create an unconnected socket object managed by ZNC.
requirements: timeout must be non-negative; semantics of 0 or negative are unknown (library-specific).
Object must be added to a socket manager before it can accept/establish connections (typical Csock usage; details not specified here).

functions.name: CZNCSock::CZNCSock
functions.signature: CZNCSock::CZNCSock(const CString& sHost, u_short port, int timeout = 60);
functions.description: Constructor that prepares a socket for a specific remote host/port with an optional timeout. Typically used prior to initiating a connection.
requirements: port must be a valid TCP/UDP port number (0–65535); usual expectation is non-zero.
timeout must be non-negative; exact behavior for special values is unspecified.
sHost should be a valid hostname or IP address.

functions.name: CZNCSock::~CZNCSock
functions.description: Destructor for CZNCSock. Cleans up socket resources as part of base Csock destruction.
requirements: Do not use the object after destruction.
Any outstanding operations using the socket should be completed or canceled before destruction (general Csock expectation).

functions.name: CZNCSock::ConvertAddress
functions.signature: int CZNCSock::ConvertAddress(const struct sockaddr_storage* pAddr, socklen_t iAddrLen, CString& sIP, u_short* piPort) const override;
functions.description: Converts a sockaddr_storage address into a human-readable IP string and port. Overrides Csock conversion to return ZNC-friendly formats.
requirements: pAddr must point to a valid sockaddr_storage; iAddrLen must match the pointed structure size for its family.
sIP is an output parameter and will be overwritten.
piPort may be null only if caller does not need the port; if non-null, it must be valid for writing a u_short.
Return value semantics (0 for success vs. non-zero) follow Csock’s convention (not detailed here).

functions.name: CZNCSock::VerifyPeerCertificate
functions.signature: int CZNCSock::VerifyPeerCertificate(int iPreVerify, X509_STORE_CTX* pStoreCTX) override;
functions.description: OpenSSL verification callback to validate the peer certificate during TLS handshake. Allows ZNC to apply custom trust rules.
requirements: Available only when compiled with HAVE_LIBSSL.
pStoreCTX must be a valid X509_STORE_CTX provided by the TLS stack during verification.
iPreVerify is the library’s pre-verification result; return value semantics follow OpenSSL/Csock expectations (non-zero to accept, zero to reject).

functions.name: CZNCSock::SSLHandShakeFinished
functions.description: Notification hook invoked after a successful TLS handshake. Can be used to finalize SSL-related state (e.g., verification results, encoding).
requirements: Available only when compiled with HAVE_LIBSSL.
Called by the SSL layer; callers should not invoke directly.

functions.name: CZNCSock::CheckSSLCert
functions.description: Performs ZNC-specific checks against the peer X509 certificate (e.g., hostname verification, fingerprint allowlist). Returns true if the certificate is acceptable.
requirements: Available only when compiled with HAVE_LIBSSL.
pCert must point to a valid X509 certificate from the peer connection.
Return value indicates acceptance (true) or rejection (false).

functions.name: CZNCSock::SSLCertError
functions.description: Virtual hook called when an SSL certificate fails validation. Default implementation does nothing; subclasses can log or enforce policy.
requirements: Available only when compiled with HAVE_LIBSSL.
pCert may be null or invalid if verification failed early; implementations should be tolerant.
Intended to be overridden by subclasses; not typically called directly by user code.

functions.name: CZNCSock::SNIConfigureClient
functions.description: Configures Server Name Indication (SNI) for a TLS client connection, potentially adjusting the hostname used for SNI.
requirements: Available only when compiled with HAVE_LIBSSL.
sHostname must contain the intended SNI host; it may be read and modified in place.
Should be called by the SSL layer during connection setup; not typically invoked by callers directly.

functions.name: CZNCSock::GetSSLPeerFingerprint
functions.description: Returns the fingerprint (hash) of the given peer certificate or the currently negotiated peer certificate if pCert is null.
requirements: Available only when compiled with HAVE_LIBSSL.
If pCert is null, the socket must be in a TLS session with a peer certificate available; otherwise result may be empty or undefined.
If pCert is non-null, it must be a valid X509 pointer.

functions.name: CZNCSock::SetHostToVerifySSL
functions.description: Sets the hostname used for SSL certificate hostname verification.
requirements: Available regardless of SSL; effective only if TLS is used.
sHost should be the expected DNS name (without port or scheme).

functions.name: CZNCSock::SetSSLTrustedPeerFingerprints
functions.description: Sets a set of trusted peer certificate fingerprints (allowlist). Any presented peer cert matching one of these fingerprints is accepted.
requirements: Fingerprints must be formatted as expected by ZNC/Csock (hash format unspecified here).
Effective only for TLS connections.

functions.name: CZNCSock::SetTrustAllCerts
functions.description: Controls whether to accept all TLS certificates without verification (insecure).
requirements: Available regardless of SSL; only has effect if TLS is used.
Setting bTrustAll to true disables standard verification; callers should ensure they understand the security implications.

functions.name: CZNCSock::GetTrustAllCerts
functions.description: Returns whether the socket is configured to trust all certificates (skip verification).

functions.name: CZNCSock::SetTrustPKI
functions.description: Controls whether platform PKI/CA trust should be honored during TLS verification.
requirements: Available regardless of SSL; only has effect if TLS is used.

functions.name: CZNCSock::GetTrustPKI
functions.description: Returns whether standard PKI/CA trust roots are used for TLS verification.

functions.name: CZNCSock::SetEncoding
functions.description: Sets the protocol text encoding for this socket (e.g., for line parsing/translation). Exact accepted values are unspecified here.
requirements: The provided encoding name must be recognized by the underlying encoding subsystem (details not present in this header).

functions.name: CZNCSock::GetRemoteIP
functions.description: Returns the remote peer IP address as a string. This override defers to Csock::GetRemoteIP().
requirements: Valid only after the socket has a remote peer (connected or accepted).

functions.name: CSockManager::CSockManager
functions.description: Constructs a ZNC socket manager responsible for creating, listening, connecting, and tracking CZNCSock instances.

functions.name: CSockManager::~CSockManager
functions.description: Destructor for the socket manager; cleans up managed sockets and any in-flight operations.
requirements: Ensure no external references to managed sockets remain after destruction.

functions.name: CSockManager::ListenHost
functions.signature: bool CSockManager::ListenHost(u_short iPort, const CString& sSockName, const CString& sBindHost, bool bSSL = false, int iMaxConns = SOMAXCONN, CZNCSock* pcSock = nullptr, u_int iTimeout = 0, EAddrType eAddr = ADDR_ALL);
functions.description: Creates a listening socket bound to a specific local host and port, with options for SSL, backlog, timeout, and address family filtering. Registers it under sSockName.
requirements: iPort must be a valid port number; usual expectation is non-zero to listen on a fixed port.
sSockName identifies the listener within the manager; must be unique within this manager (implied by AddSock semantics, not specified here).
sBindHost may be empty to bind all interfaces.
iMaxConns must be >= 0; SOMAXCONN is typical default.
pcSock, if provided, must be a valid CZNCSock prepared for listening. Behavior when pcSock is null depends on TSocketManager::Listen (unspecified here).
eAddr affects AF selection only when compiled with IPv6 support.

functions.name: CSockManager::ListenAll
functions.signature: bool CSockManager::ListenAll(u_short iPort, const CString& sSockName, bool bSSL = false, int iMaxConns = SOMAXCONN, CZNCSock* pcSock = nullptr, u_int iTimeout = 0, EAddrType eAddr = ADDR_ALL);
functions.description: Convenience wrapper to listen on all local interfaces for the given port, delegating to ListenHost with an empty bind host.
requirements: Same as ListenHost except sBindHost is empty to select all interfaces.

functions.name: CSockManager::ListenRand
functions.signature: u_short CSockManager::ListenRand(const CString& sSockName, const CString& sBindHost, bool bSSL = false, int iMaxConns = SOMAXCONN, CZNCSock* pcSock = nullptr, u_int iTimeout = 0, EAddrType eAddr = ADDR_ALL);
functions.description: Creates a listening socket on an ephemeral (random) port bound to sBindHost, registers it by name, and returns the chosen port.
requirements: sSockName identifies the listener; should be unique within the manager.
pcSock, if provided, must be valid for listening. Behavior when null is determined by Listen (unspecified).
Returned port is 0 if listen failed.

functions.name: CSockManager::ListenAllRand
functions.signature: u_short CSockManager::ListenAllRand(const CString& sSockName, bool bSSL = false, int iMaxConns = SOMAXCONN, CZNCSock* pcSock = nullptr, u_int iTimeout = 0, EAddrType eAddr = ADDR_ALL);
functions.description: Convenience to listen on an ephemeral port on all interfaces; returns the selected port.
requirements: Same requirements as ListenRand; sBindHost is empty.

functions.name: CSockManager::Connect
functions.signature: void CSockManager::Connect(const CString& sHostname, u_short iPort, const CString& sSockName, int iTimeout = 60, bool bSSL = false, const CString& sBindHost = "", CZNCSock* pcSock = nullptr);
functions.description: Initiates an outbound connection to sHostname:iPort, optionally using SSL and binding to a local address. Registers the socket under sSockName.
requirements: sHostname must be a valid hostname or IP address.
iPort must be a valid non-zero port.
iTimeout should be non-negative.
If provided, sBindHost must be a valid local address to bind.

functions.name: CUser::CUser
functions.description: Constructs a CUser instance with the given username. Initializes user-related state and defaults.
requirements: sUsername must represent a valid username for later use; call IsValidUsername() or MakeCleanUsername() if unsure.

functions.name: CUser::~CUser
functions.description: Destroys the CUser instance and releases associated resources (networks, clients, modules, etc.), if owned.
requirements: All external references to this CUser and its owned objects must be invalidated before destruction to avoid use-after-free.

functions.name: CUser::ParseConfig
functions.description: Parses and applies user configuration from the provided config object, reporting errors in sError on failure.
requirements: Config must be a valid, initialized pointer.
sError is used for error reporting and will be modified on failure.
Returns true on success; false on failure with sError describing the issue.

functions.name: CUser::SaltedHash
functions.signature: static CString CUser::SaltedHash(const CString& sPass, const CString& sSalt)
functions.description: Returns a salted hash of the given password using ZNC’s configured hashing routine (forwards to CUtils::SaltedHash).
requirements: sPass and sSalt are treated as byte strings; no encoding assumptions are documented.
Deterministic for the same inputs; callers should provide a properly generated salt.

functions.name: CUser::ToConfig
functions.description: Serializes the current user into a CConfig object representing its configuration.
requirements: Returned CConfig reflects the current CUser state at call time.

functions.name: CUser::CheckPass
functions.description: Verifies the supplied password against the stored hash and may upgrade the hash method on success.
requirements: sPass is the plaintext password to check.
Returns true if the password matches; false otherwise.
May change internal password storage to a stronger hash upon success.

functions.name: CUser::AddAllowedHost
functions.description: Adds a host mask to the set of allowed hosts for this user.
requirements: sHostMask should be a valid host mask string as used by ZNC/IRC.
Returns true if added; false if already present or invalid.

functions.name: CUser::RemAllowedHost
functions.description: Removes a host mask from the set of allowed hosts for this user.
requirements: sHostMask should match an existing allowed host mask.
Returns true if removed; false if it was not present.

functions.name: CUser::ClearAllowedHosts
functions.description: Clears all allowed host masks for this user.
requirements: After calling, no hosts will be allowed unless re-added; ensure this will not lock out legitimate access.

functions.name: CUser::IsHostAllowed
functions.description: Checks whether the given host matches any of the user’s allowed host masks.
requirements: sHost should be the full host (e.g., user@host/IP) format expected by ZNC.
Returns true if allowed; false otherwise.

functions.name: CUser::IsValid
functions.signature: bool CUser::IsValid(CString& sErrMsg, bool bSkipPass = false) const
functions.description: Validates the user’s configuration and state; optionally skips password validation.
requirements: sErrMsg is used for error reporting and will be modified on failure.
If bSkipPass is false, a valid password/hash must be set.
Returns true if valid; false otherwise with sErrMsg explaining why.

functions.name: CUser::IsValidUsername
functions.description: Checks whether the supplied username meets ZNC’s validity rules.
requirements: sUsername is validated against ZNC’s allowed character and format rules.
Returns true if valid; false otherwise.

functions.name: CUser::IsValidUserName
functions.description: Deprecated alias of IsValidUsername(). Validates a username string.
requirements: Prefer using IsValidUsername().
Returns true if valid; false otherwise.

functions.name: CUser::MakeCleanUsername
functions.description: Normalizes/sanitizes the supplied username into a clean form acceptable by ZNC.
requirements: Input may be modified (e.g., characters removed or case adjusted) to satisfy naming rules.

functions.name: CUser::MakeCleanUserName
functions.description: Deprecated alias of MakeCleanUsername(). Returns a sanitized username.
requirements: Prefer using MakeCleanUsername().

functions.name: CUser::GetModules
functions.description: Returns a modifiable reference to the user’s module manager.
requirements: Returned reference must not be used after the CUser is destroyed.

functions.name: CUser::AddNetwork
functions.signature: CIRCNetwork* CUser::AddNetwork(const CString& sNetwork, CString& sErrorRet)
functions.description: Creates and adds a new IRC network with the given name to the user. On failure, returns nullptr and sets sErrorRet.
requirements: sNetwork is the network name to create.
sErrorRet will be set with a reason on failure.
Returns non-null pointer on success.

functions.name: CUser::DeleteNetwork
functions.description: Deletes the IRC network with the given name from the user.
requirements: sNetwork must match an existing network name.
Returns true on successful deletion; false if not found or cannot delete.

functions.name: CUser::RemoveNetwork
functions.description: Removes the given CIRCNetwork from the user’s list (without necessarily deleting it).
requirements: pNetwork must be a valid pointer to a network currently associated with this user.

functions.name: CUser::FindNetwork
functions.description: Finds a network by name and returns a pointer to it, or nullptr if not found.
requirements: sNetwork must be the exact network name as stored.

functions.name: CUser::GetNetworks
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the vector of this user’s IRC networks.
requirements: Do not modify the returned container or its elements through this reference.
Reference becomes invalid when the user object is destroyed or networks are changed.

functions.name: CUser::HasSpaceForNewNetwork
functions.description: Indicates whether the user can add another network (based on configured limits).
requirements: Returns true if adding a new network is currently allowed; false otherwise.

functions.name: CUser::PutUser
functions.signature: bool CUser::PutUser(const CString& sLine, CClient* pClient = nullptr, CClient* pSkipClient = nullptr)
functions.description: Sends a line to the user’s connected client(s). Optionally target a specific client and/or skip one client.
requirements: sLine is a single IRC-formatted line to send.
pClient, if non-null, selects a specific client to send to.
pSkipClient, if non-null, will be excluded.
Returns true if at least one client was written to; false otherwise.

functions.name: CUser::PutAllUser
functions.signature: bool CUser::PutAllUser(const CString& sLine, CClient* pClient = nullptr, CClient* pSkipClient = nullptr)
functions.description: Deprecated. Forwards to PutUser() to send a line to user clients.
requirements: Use PutUser() instead.

functions.name: CUser::PutStatus
functions.signature: bool CUser::PutStatus(const CString& sLine, CClient* pClient = nullptr, CClient* pSkipClient = nullptr)
functions.description: Sends a line to the user’s status window across client(s).
requirements: sLine must be status-appropriate content.
Optional pClient targets one client; pSkipClient excludes one.
Returns true if delivered to at least one client.

functions.name: CUser::PutStatusNotice
functions.signature: bool CUser::PutStatusNotice(const CString& sLine, CClient* pClient = nullptr, CClient* pSkipClient = nullptr)
functions.description: Sends a notice to the user’s status window across client(s).
requirements: Same targeting semantics as PutStatus().
Returns true if delivered to at least one client.

functions.name: CUser::PutModule
functions.signature: bool CUser::PutModule(const CString& sModule, const CString& sLine, CClient* pClient = nullptr, CClient* pSkipClient = nullptr)
functions.description: Sends a line from a specific module to the user’s client(s).
requirements: sModule is the module identifier to prefix or route the message.
Returns true if delivered to at least one client.

functions.name: CUser::PutModNotice
functions.signature: bool CUser::PutModNotice(const CString& sModule, const CString& sLine, CClient* pClient = nullptr, CClient* pSkipClient = nullptr)
functions.description: Sends a module-scoped notice to the user’s client(s).
requirements: sModule names the originating module.
Returns true if delivered to at least one client.

functions.name: CUser::IsUserAttached
functions.description: Returns whether at least one client is currently attached to this user.
requirements: None.

functions.name: CUser::UserConnected
functions.description: Notifies the user object that a client has connected/attached.
requirements: pClient must be a valid client pointer representing the attaching client.

functions.name: CUser::UserDisconnected
functions.description: Notifies the user object that a client has disconnected/detached.
requirements: pClient must be a valid client pointer representing the detaching client.

functions.name: CUser::GetLocalDCCIP
functions.description: Returns the local IP address to use for DCC connections, considering user-specific settings.
requirements: None stated.

functions.name: CUser::ExpandString

requirements: sStr may contain placeholders recognized by ZNC.

functions.name: CUser::AddTimestamp

requirements: Behavior is controlled by SetTimestampFormat(), SetTimestampAppend(), and SetTimestampPrepend().

functions.name: CUser::CloneNetworks
functions.description: Copies network configurations from another user into this user.
requirements: User must be an initialized CUser whose networks can be read.
Destination user must have capacity (see HasSpaceForNewNetwork()).

functions.name: CUser::Clone
functions.signature: bool CUser::Clone(const CUser& User, CString& sErrorRet, bool bCloneNetworks = true)
functions.description: Clones the configuration (and optionally networks) from another user to this user, reporting errors on failure.
requirements: User is the source CUser to clone from.
sErrorRet receives an error description on failure.
If bCloneNetworks is true, ensure capacity for networks.
Returns true on success; false on failure.

functions.name: CUser::BounceAllClients
functions.description: Disconnects and/or reattaches all clients associated with this user (e.g., during reconfiguration).
requirements: Clients may temporarily lose connection; ensure caller intends to bounce all clients.

functions.name: CUser::AddBytesRead
functions.description: Increments the counter of bytes read for this user by u.
requirements: u is added as an unsigned 64-bit value.

functions.name: CUser::AddBytesWritten
functions.description: Increments the counter of bytes written for this user by u.
requirements: u is added as an unsigned 64-bit value.

functions.name: CUser::SetNick

requirements: s should be a valid IRC nickname per server rules.

functions.name: CUser::SetAltNick
functions.description: Sets the alternate nickname for this user.
requirements: s should be a valid IRC nickname per server rules.

functions.name: CUser::SetIdent
functions.description: Sets the ident/username (IRC user field) for this user.
requirements: s should follow IRC ident formatting rules if enforced.

functions.name: CUser::SetRealName
functions.description: Sets the real name (gecos) field for this user.
requirements: None stated.

functions.name: CUser::SetBindHost

functions.name: CUser::SetDCCBindHost

requirements: s is a hostname/IP that should be valid.

functions.name: CUser::SetPass

functions.description: Sets the user’s password using the specified hash type and optional salt.
requirements: s is the password in plaintext or already-hashed depending on eHash handling (implementation-specific).
eHash selects the hash algorithm (e.g., HASH_MD5, HASH_SHA256, HASH_ARGON2ID).

functions.name: CUser::SetMultiClients

requirements: b = true to allow multiple clients; false to restrict to one.

functions.name: CUser::SetDenyLoadMod

requirements: b = true to deny module loading for this user.

functions.name: CUser::SetAdmin

requirements: Admin privileges affect permission checks across ZNC.

functions.name: CUser::SetDenySetBindHost

functions.name: CUser::SetDenySetIdent

functions.name: CUser::SetDenySetCTCPReplies

functions.name: CUser::SetStatusPrefix

functions.name: CUser::SetDefaultChanModes

functions.name: CUser::SetClientEncoding

functions.name: CUser::SetQuitMsg

requirements: None stated.

functions.name: CUser::AddCTCPReply
functions.signature: bool CUser::AddCTCPReply(const CString& sCTCP, const CString& sReply)

functions.name: CUser::DelCTCPReply

functions.name: CUser::SetBufferCount

functions.description: Deprecated. Sets the unified buffer count; superseded by SetChanBufferSize() and SetQueryBufferSize().
requirements: Prefer using SetChanBufferSize() and SetQueryBufferSize().
u is the new buffer count value.
bForce may allow bypassing limits depending on implementation.
Returns true on success; false otherwise.

functions.name: CUser::SetChanBufferSize

functions.name: CUser::SetAutoClearQueryBuffer

requirements: b = true to clear buffers automatically after delivery or on conditions defined by ZNC.

functions.name: CUser::SetLanguage
functions.description: Sets the user’s preferred language for translations.
requirements: s is a valid language identifier known to ZNC.
Returns true on success; false on invalid/unsupported language.

functions.name: CUser::SetBeingDeleted
functions.description: Marks the user as being deleted; affects behavior of ongoing operations.
requirements: Intended for internal lifecycle management.

functions.name: CUser::SetTimestampFormat
functions.description: Sets the strftime-like timestamp format string used for message timestamps.
requirements: s must be a valid format string accepted by ZNC’s timestamping.

functions.name: CUser::SetTimestampAppend
functions.description: Enables appending timestamps to messages.
requirements: Mutually exclusive with prepend in typical usage; see SetTimestampPrepend().

functions.name: CUser::SetTimestampPrepend
functions.description: Enables prepending timestamps to messages.

functions.name: CChan::CChan
functions.signature: CChan::CChan(const CString& sName, CIRCNetwork* pNetwork, bool bInConfig, CConfig* pConfig = nullptr)
functions.description: Constructor for a channel object bound to an IRC network. Initializes a channel with a name, associates it with a network, notes whether it is present in the config, and optionally consumes configuration data. Use this to create a channel before joining or managing its state.
requirements: pNetwork must point to a valid CIRCNetwork instance (must not be null).
sName should be a valid IRC channel name (format specifics not documented here).

functions.name: CChan::~CChan

functions.name: CChan::Reset

functions.name: CChan::ToConfig

requirements: The CChan instance must be valid.

functions.name: CChan::Clone

functions.name: CChan::Cycle

functions.name: CChan::JoinUser

functions.name: CChan::AttachUser

requirements: If provided, pClient must point to a valid CClient instance that remains alive for the duration of the call.

functions.name: CChan::DetachUser
functions.description: Detaches the current client/session from this channel. Typically used when a client disconnects to stop sending channel events/buffers to it.
requirements: The CChan must currently have an attached client for detachment to have effect (not enforced by signature).

functions.name: CChan::OnWho
