functions.name: CChan::SetModes

functions.name: CChan::AddMode

functions.name: CChan::ClearNicks

functions.name: CChan::AddNicks

functions.name: CChan::AddNick

functions.name: CChan::RemNick

functions.name: CChan::GetBuffer

requirements: If provided, ts must point to a valid timeval structure for timestamping.
mssTags provides message tags; may be empty.

functions.name: CChan::ClearBuffer

functions.name: CChan::SendBuffer

functions.name: CChan::SendBuffer

functions.name: CChan::GetPermStr

functions.description: Destructor. Cleans up by invoking close2() with the stored PID and the current read/write sockets, then marks the internal descriptors as invalid. Intended to ensure the child process and associated file descriptors are properly cleaned up when the object goes out of scope.
requirements: The object must not be used after destruction (general C++ object lifetime rule).
Resources (child process and FDs) are relinquished during destruction; callers that need explicit control should invoke Kill()/close2() before destruction (inferred from cleanup behavior).

functions.name: CExecSock::popen2
functions.signature: int CExecSock::popen2(int& iReadFD, int& iWriteFD, const CString& sCommand);
functions.description: Creates a child process to execute sCommand and sets up two file descriptors for IPC (typically a read FD for data from the child and a write FD for data to the child). Returns the child PID on success, or -1 on failure. Exact stream mapping (stdout/stderr) is not documented here and is therefore unknown. This function is declared here and defined elsewhere.
requirements: iReadFD and iWriteFD must be lvalue references provided by the caller; on success they are assigned valid file descriptors (inferred from int& parameters).
sCommand should be a non-empty, valid command string resolvable by the system shell or exec variant used (inferred from purpose).
Caller must check the return value; -1 indicates failure (inferred from common popen2 semantics and Execute() usage).

On success, the caller is responsible for eventually closing the returned file descriptors and reaping/terminating the child process (e.g., via close2 or equivalent) to avoid resource leaks (inferred from existence of close2).

functions.name: CExecSock::close2
functions.signature: void CExecSock::close2(int iPid, int iReadFD, int iWriteFD);
functions.description: Cleans up resources associated with a process created by popen2(): closes the provided file descriptors and performs process-related cleanup for iPid (details such as wait/kill are unspecified in this header and thus unknown). Declared here and defined elsewhere.
requirements: iPid should be the PID previously returned by popen2() (inferred from naming and usage in the destructor).
iReadFD and iWriteFD should be valid (open) file descriptors obtained from popen2(); passing already-closed or invalid FDs can lead to errors or undefined behavior (inferred from purpose).
Should not be called multiple times for the same pid/FD set to avoid double-closing and duplicate cleanup (inferred from cleanup semantics).

unharnessable_functions.name: CZNC::CZNC
unharnessable_functions.reason: Constructors cannot be called as free functions in a harness and CZNC is intended to be created via the singleton CreateInstance() API.

unharnessable_functions.name: CZNC::~CZNC
unharnessable_functions.reason: Destructors cannot be directly invoked in a harness and lifetime is managed by the CZNC singleton APIs.

unharnessable_functions.name: CZNC::Loop
unharnessable_functions.reason: Runs the main event loop and would block indefinitely, which is incompatible with a fast fuzzer harness.

unharnessable_functions.name: CZNC::WritePidFile
unharnessable_functions.reason: Writes to the internal PID file path which cannot be safely directed to a sandbox without prior CZNC initialization.

unharnessable_functions.name: CZNC::DeletePidFile
unharnessable_functions.reason: Deletes the internal PID file whose location depends on prior CZNC initialization, risking unintended filesystem side effects.

unharnessable_functions.name: CZNC::WaitForChildLock
unharnessable_functions.reason: Blocks waiting on an external lock condition, which is unsuitable for fuzzing due to unbounded wait.

unharnessable_functions.name: CZNC::InitDirs
unharnessable_functions.reason: Modifies process-wide directory configuration and may create directories on the host filesystem, which is unsafe for the harness.

unharnessable_functions.name: CZNC::OnBoot
unharnessable_functions.reason: Performs broad system initialization including sockets and modules which can block or create persistent external state.

unharnessable_functions.name: CZNC::WriteConfig
unharnessable_functions.reason: Writes the in-memory configuration to a process-defined path, potentially affecting host filesystem outside the fuzz sandbox.

unharnessable_functions.name: CZNC::CreateInstance
unharnessable_functions.reason: Manipulates the global singleton and conflicts with the fuzzer’s object pool lifetime management.

unharnessable_functions.name: CZNC::Get
unharnessable_functions.reason: Accessing the global singleton interferes with the fuzzer-managed CZNC instances and may create aliasing/lifetime issues.

unharnessable_functions.name: CZNC::DestroyInstance
unharnessable_functions.reason: Destroying the global singleton can invalidate CZNC pointers in the fuzzer pool, risking use-after-free.

unharnessable_functions.name: CZNC::AddListener
unharnessable_functions.reason: Adding a listener may bind sockets and perform blocking network operations which are unsuitable for the fuzzer environment.

unharnessable_functions.name: CZNC::AddTCPListener
unharnessable_functions.reason: Creates and binds TCP sockets with potential blocking and environmental side effects not suitable for fuzzing.

unharnessable_functions.name: CZNC::AddUnixListener
unharnessable_functions.reason: Creates UNIX domain sockets and manipulates filesystem permissions, causing external side effects unsuitable for fuzzing.

unharnessable_functions.name: CZNC::LeakConnectQueueTimer
unharnessable_functions.reason: This function must only be called from CConnectQueueTimer::~CConnectQueueTimer(), which we cannot safely simulate in a fuzzer harness.

unharnessable_functions.name: ZNCModuleEntry
unharnessable_functions.reason: Module entry point is defined by individual modules and not callable meaningfully from a generic fuzzer TU without a concrete module implementation.

unharnessable_functions.name: TModLoad
unharnessable_functions.reason: Template function requires a concrete module type parameter and construction context, which cannot be generically instantiated by the fuzzer.

unharnessable_functions.name: CIRCSock::SSLCertError
unharnessable_functions.reason: Depends on HAVE_LIBSSL and X509 type; not portable to harness without SSL build and certificate objects.

unharnessable_functions.name: CZNCSock::VerifyPeerCertificate
unharnessable_functions.reason: This method is only available when compiled with HAVE_LIBSSL and cannot be safely called across builds without conditional compilation.

unharnessable_functions.name: CZNCSock::SSLHandShakeFinished
unharnessable_functions.reason: This hook exists only with HAVE_LIBSSL enabled and invoking it unconditionally is not portable across build configurations.

unharnessable_functions.name: CZNCSock::CheckSSLCert
unharnessable_functions.reason: The function depends on OpenSSL types and is compiled only with HAVE_LIBSSL, so it cannot be reliably exercised without conditional guards.

unharnessable_functions.name: CZNCSock::SSLCertError
unharnessable_functions.reason: This SSL-specific hook is present only under HAVE_LIBSSL and cannot be invoked portably without conditional compilation.

unharnessable_functions.name: CZNCSock::SNIConfigureClient
unharnessable_functions.reason: SNI configuration is compiled only when HAVE_LIBSSL is defined, making it unsafe to harness unconditionally.

unharnessable_functions.name: CZNCSock::GetSSLPeerFingerprint
unharnessable_functions.reason: This accessor requires SSL support (HAVE_LIBSSL) and cannot be safely used without build-time conditionals.

unharnessable_functions.name: CSocket::CSocket
unharnessable_functions.reason: Requires a valid CModule* owner which cannot be constructed under the current fuzzer model.

unharnessable_functions.name: CSocket::~CSocket
unharnessable_functions.reason: Requires a valid CSocket instance which in turn needs a CModule*, unavailable to construct safely here.

unharnessable_functions.name: CSocket::ReachedMaxBuffer
unharnessable_functions.reason: Cannot obtain a valid CSocket instance without constructing a CModule*, which is unsupported in this harness.

unharnessable_functions.name: CSocket::SockError
unharnessable_functions.reason: Cannot safely instantiate CSocket (needs CModule*) to invoke this callback under current constraints.

unharnessable_functions.name: CSocket::ConnectionFrom
unharnessable_functions.reason: Depends on a live CSocket instance owned by a CModule, which we cannot construct.

unharnessable_functions.name: CSocket::Connect
unharnessable_functions.reason: Member requires a valid CSocket associated with a CModule, which we cannot create in this environment.

unharnessable_functions.name: CSocket::Listen
unharnessable_functions.reason: Member requires a valid CSocket associated with a CModule, which we cannot create in this environment.

unharnessable_functions.name: CSocket::ConnectUnix
unharnessable_functions.reason: Member requires a valid CSocket associated with a CModule, which we cannot create in this environment.

unharnessable_functions.name: CSocket::ListenUnix
unharnessable_functions.reason: Member requires a valid CSocket associated with a CModule, which we cannot create in this environment.

unharnessable_functions.name: CSocket::ConstructSockName
unharnessable_functions.reason: Cannot call without a valid CSocket object, which needs a CModule we can’t construct here.

unharnessable_functions.name: CSocket::GetModule
unharnessable_functions.reason: Requires a valid CSocket instance which depends on constructing a CModule, not feasible here.

unharnessable_functions.name: CSocket::t_s
unharnessable_functions.reason: Translation helper is a CSocket member; we cannot construct CSocket due to unavailable CModule dependency.

unharnessable_functions.name: CIRCSocket::IcuExtToUCallback
unharnessable_functions.reason: Depends on ICU types and HAVE_ICU build flag; cannot be safely invoked or constructed in this fuzzer environment.

unharnessable_functions.name: CIRCSocket::IcuExtFromUCallback
unharnessable_functions.reason: Depends on ICU types and HAVE_ICU build flag; cannot be safely invoked or constructed in this fuzzer environment.

unharnessable_functions.name: CListener::CListener
unharnessable_functions.reason: CListener is abstract (pure virtual Listen), so its constructor cannot be directly invoked to instantiate an object.

unharnessable_functions.name: CListener::Listen
unharnessable_functions.reason: This is a pure virtual function on CListener and cannot be called directly; only concrete overrides exist.

unharnessable_functions.name: CListener::SetupSSL
unharnessable_functions.reason: SetupSSL is a protected helper and cannot be safely invoked from an external fuzzer stub without subclass access.

unharnessable_functions.name: InitTime
unharnessable_functions.reason: This method is private to CMessage and cannot be called from a fuzzer stub.

unharnessable_functions.name: InitType
unharnessable_functions.reason: This method is private to CMessage and cannot be called from a fuzzer stub.

unharnessable_functions.name: operator<<
unharnessable_functions.reason: The stream operator is only available when GTEST_FAIL is defined at compile time, which the fuzzer environment does not guarantee.

unharnessable_functions.name: CNick::GetCommonChans
unharnessable_functions.reason: Requires a valid CIRCNetwork* which cannot be safely constructed or guaranteed by the fuzzer runtime under current constraints.

unharnessable_functions.name: CHTTPSock
unharnessable_functions.reason: CHTTPSock is an abstract class (pure virtual methods), so its constructor cannot be directly invoked to create an instance.

unharnessable_functions.name: GetSockObj
unharnessable_functions.reason: The pure virtual factory depends on subclass-specific allocation and returns an opaque Csock* that cannot be safely owned or freed by the fuzzer.

unharnessable_functions.name: PrintErrorPage
unharnessable_functions.reason: The method is protected in CWebSock (using-declaration marks CHTTPSock::PrintErrorPage as protected), preventing safe external invocation from a harness.

data_types.description: A string representing a hostname or an IRC-style hostmask. Examples: "example.com", "user@host", "*@example.org", or CIDR-like/wildcard notations accepted by ZNC (e.g., "192.168.*").
A path to a file or directory, absolute or relative, using the host OS path syntax. May include directories and filename components.
Plaintext content of a ZNC configuration file (znc.conf format), including key-value pairs and nested sections as used by ZNC. Arbitrary text may be provided to test the parser.
An arbitrary short string appended to a filename to form a backup name. Typically contains characters safe for filenames (e.g., ".bak"), but fuzzing may include any bytes.
A string representing a DNS hostname or an IP address (IPv4 or IPv6). Examples: "proxy.example.com", "203.0.113.5", "2001:db8::1".
Arbitrary user-visible text content without specific format constraints. May include spaces, punctuation, and control characters.
A user login name string as used by ZNC. Typically alphanumeric with limited punctuation, but fuzzing may include arbitrary strings.
An authentication secret string. Treated as opaque bytes; may contain any characters.
A short, human-readable identifier such as a skin name or status prefix. Generally ASCII but not restricted by format.
A cipher suite selection string in OpenSSL format, e.g., "HIGH:!aNULL:@STRENGTH". May be arbitrary for fuzzing, with validation done by the SSL library.
A protocol selection string controlling allowed SSL/TLS versions in ZNC, e.g., "TLSv1.2", "TLSv1.2+TLSv1.3", or other build-dependent tokens.
The name of a ZNC module to load/find/update. Typically a short identifier (e.g., "webadmin"), without path separators.

A single IRC protocol line as sent by a client or to a server. Typically begins with an optional prefix ":nick!user@host", followed by a command (e.g., PRIVMSG, JOIN, NICK, numeric), parameters separated by spaces, and an optional trailing parameter starting with ':' that may contain spaces. Max length is commonly 512 bytes per RFCs.
The inner text of a CTCP message (without the surrounding \x01 delimiters). Examples include ACTION, VERSION, PING, TIME; payload may include a command and optional arguments (e.g., "ACTION waves").
An unparsed IRC message string used to construct a CMessage object. It may include a prefix, command, parameters, and tags per IRCv3 (e.g., "@time=...;tag=val :nick!u@h PRIVMSG #chan :hello").

Name of an IRCv3 capability as used in CAP negotiation, e.g., "server-time", "message-tags", "batch", "account-notify", "away-notify". Usually lowercase with hyphens; vendor-prefixed names may include a slash.
The key/name of an IRCv3 message tag (without value), e.g., "time", "batch", "label", or vendor tags like "+draft/label". Typically lowercase and may include vendor prefixes.

An IRC nickname string. Usually limited to allowed characters per server (letters, digits, special characters like -[]\`^{}_). Often up to ~9 or more characters, case-insensitive per RFC, without spaces.

Opaque bytes for IRC SASL AUTHENTICATE payload prior to Base64 encoding. For PLAIN it is typically "authzid\0authcid\0passwd"; other mechanisms have different formats. Chunk may be split across multiple messages.

A textual representation of a certificate fingerprint, typically a sequence of hexadecimal byte pairs separated by colons (e.g., "12:34:AB:CD:..."), or contiguous hex which may be normalized. Case-insensitive hex digits allowed; length commonly corresponds to SHA-1 (20 bytes -> 59 chars with colons) or SHA-256 (32 bytes -> 95 chars with colons).
Arbitrary bytes representing part of an HTTP request stream (headers and/or body). May include partial lines, binary payload, or be empty. Used to feed socket parsers.
A single HTTP request or header line without CR/LF terminators. For example: "GET /path HTTP/1.1" or "Host: example.com". No embedded newlines.
The request target portion of an HTTP request, typically a path and optional query (e.g., "/index.html?x=1"). No CR/LF.
An HTTP header field name token (e.g., "Content-Type", "X-Test"). Must not contain control characters or CR/LF.
The value part of an HTTP header field (e.g., "text/html; charset=utf-8"). Must not contain CR/LF.
A media type string for HTTP Content-Type, such as "text/html", "application/json; charset=utf-8".
A URL used in HTTP redirects; may be absolute (e.g., "https://example.com/a") or relative (e.g., "/a?b=c"). No CR/LF.
application/x-www-form-urlencoded parameter string, e.g., "a=1&b=2&b=3" with percent-encoding for special characters.
A cookie key/name token as used in HTTP Cookie and Set-Cookie headers. Should avoid control characters and separators.
Opaque cookie value string to be set in Set-Cookie. May include URL-safe characters; control characters and CR/LF are disallowed.
The key/name for a query or form parameter in HTTP (GET/POST). Typically ASCII token without CR/LF.
A gettext-style domain identifier, such as "znc" or "znc-<module>", selecting a translation catalog.
An optional gettext context string used to disambiguate identical source strings in translation catalogs.
A locale/language identifier such as "en", "en_US", "de_DE". Often in the form ll or ll_CC using POSIX locale conventions.

A string which is Base64-encoded per RFC 4648 (alphabet A–Z, a–z, 0–9, +, / with optional = padding). May include arbitrary valid or invalid Base64 for robustness testing; decoders typically expect valid Base64 but fuzzing may supply malformed inputs.

An IRC channel identifier string, typically beginning with a prefix such as # or & (e.g., #znc, &local). May include letters, digits, and certain symbols per server rules. No spaces; case-insensitive by RFC. Used wherever a channel target is required.

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces a bytes buffer that represents a newline-separated
# corpus of interesting filesystem paths to seed FUZZ_PARAM_STR and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME
# in the target fuzzers. The fuzzer environment typically interprets the provided
# buffer to create files for FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME and to supply strings for FUZZ_PARAM_STR.
# We therefore include a wide variety of path shapes (absolute, relative, with dot
# components, URI-like prefixes for web paths, unix socket-like names, etc.).
# The content is deterministic given the seed, yet includes randomness to diversify runs.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_.,@+="

def rand_name(rng: random.Random, minlen: int = 1, maxlen: int = 12) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(minlen, maxlen)
    return ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(n))

def rand_ext(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    return rng.choice([
        "conf", "cfg", "txt", "log", "ini", "dat", "json", "xml",
        "pem", "crt", "key", "sock", "tmp", "lock"
    ])

def unix_mode_str(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # 3 or 4-digit octal-like string
    digits = "01234567"
    length = rng.choice([3, 4])
    return ''.join(rng.choice(digits) for _ in range(length))

def maybe_prefix(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    return rng.choice([
        "", "./", "../", "../../", "/", "/tmp/", "/var/tmp/", "/var/run/", "/run/",
        "./.", ".//", "~/",  # shell-like; some code may treat ~ as literal
    ])

def web_prefix(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # For CWebSock URIs and template paths
    parts = ["/"]
    segs = rng.randint(1, 3)
    for _ in range(segs):
        parts.append(rand_name(rng, 1, 8))
        parts.append("/")
    return ''.join(parts).rstrip('/') or "/"

def build_relative_paths(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    paths = []
    # Simple relative files
    for _ in range(6):
        paths.append(f"{rand_name(rng)}.{rand_ext(rng)}")
    # Dot components
    for _ in range(4):
        parts = [rng.choice([".", "..", "..."]) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3))]
        parts += [rand_name(rng, 1, 6), rand_name(rng, 1, 6) + "." + rand_ext(rng)]
        paths.append("/".join(parts))
    # Subdirectories
    for _ in range(5):
        depth = rng.randint(1, 4)
        parts = [rand_name(rng, 1, 8) for _ in range(depth)]
        leaf = rand_name(rng, 1, 8) + "." + rand_ext(rng)
        paths.append("/".join(parts + [leaf]))
    # Named pipes/sockets-like names
    for base in ["znc", "sock", "unix", "listener", "registry"]:
        paths.append(base + ".sock")
        paths.append(base + ".lock")
    return paths

def build_absolute_paths(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    paths = []
    # Common absolute bases
    bases = ["/tmp", "/var/tmp", "/var/run", "/run", "/etc", "/usr/local/etc", "/dev/shm"]
    for b in bases:
        # plain file
        paths.append(f"{b}/{rand_name(rng)}.{rand_ext(rng)}")
        # nested
        depth = rng.randint(1, 3)
        parts = [rand_name(rng, 1, 8) for _ in range(depth)]
        leaf = rand_name(rng, 1, 8) + "." + rand_ext(rng)
        paths.append(f"{b}/" + "/".join(parts + [leaf]))
        # directory path (for listeners etc.)
        paths.append(f"{b}/" + "/".join(parts))
    # Unix socket style under run
    for name in ["znc", "http", "irc", "web"]:
        paths.append(f"/run/{name}.sock")
        paths.append(f"/var/run/{name}-{rng.randint(1,9999)}.sock")
    return paths

def build_uri_and_template(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    paths = []
    for _ in range(6):
        prefix = web_prefix(rng)
        tail = rand_name(rng, 1, 10)
        paths.append(f"{prefix}/{tail}")
        # add query strings for CSRF tests
        qkey = rng.choice(["csrf", "token", "id", "x"]) 
        qval = rand_name(rng, 6, 12)
        paths.append(f"{prefix}/{tail}?{qkey}={qval}")
    # Skin/template-like
    for skin in ["skin", "default", "material", "classic"]:
        paths.append(f"/skins/{skin}/index.tmpl")
        paths.append(f"/skins/{skin}/main.css")
    return paths

def build_mixed_weird(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    paths = []
    # Include modes/gid-like strings as standalone entries for APIs that expect them
    for _ in range(5):
        paths.append(unix_mode_str(rng))
    # Identifiers or names used by various APIs
    for _ in range(6):
        paths.append(rand_name(rng, 3, 10))
    # Paths with prefixes and redundancies
    for _ in range(6):
        p = maybe_prefix(rng) + rand_name(rng, 1, 8)
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            p += "/" + rand_name(rng, 1, 8) + "." + rand_ext(rng)
        paths.append(p)
    # Include some absolute with dotdot components (normalized by consumers)
    for _ in range(4):
        parts = ["/tmp", rand_name(rng, 1, 6), "..", rand_name(rng, 1, 6), rand_name(rng, 1, 6)+"."+rand_ext(rng)]
        paths.append("/".join([parts[0]] + parts[1:]))
    return paths

def dedup_keep_order(items: List[str]) -> List[str]:
    seen = set()
    out = []
    for it in items:
        if it not in seen:
            seen.add(it)
            out.append(it)
    return out

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    items: List[str] = []
    # Prioritize valid existing paths to improve success chances for operations
    # that require real files. Provide a few well-known readable files if present.
    likely_exist = [
        "/etc/hosts", "/etc/services", "/etc/passwd", "/proc/self/cmdline",
    ]
    for p in likely_exist:
        if os.path.exists(p):
            items.append(p)
    # Also include current working directory
    try:
        cwd = os.getcwd()
        if cwd:
            items.append(cwd)
    except Exception:
        pass

    items += build_relative_paths(rng)
    items += build_absolute_paths(rng)
    items += build_uri_and_template(rng)
    items += build_mixed_weird(rng)

    # Add a few randomized SSL-related filenames for SetSSLCertFile and friends
    for base in ["znc", "server", "client", "testcert"]:
        items.append(f"/tmp/{base}-{rng.randint(1,99999)}.pem")
        items.append(f"/tmp/{base}-{rng.randint(1,99999)}.crt")
        items.append(f"/tmp/{base}-{rng.randint(1,99999)}.key")

    # Limit total size and deduplicate
    items = dedup_keep_order(items)

    # Shuffle a bit but keep deterministic order with seed
    rng.shuffle(items)

    # Join as newline-separated to allow consumers to split
    data = "\n".join(items)
    b = data.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    if len(b) > MAX_TOTAL:
        b = b[:MAX_TOTAL]
        # Ensure we don't cut mid-line in a way that breaks parses: trim to last newline
        last_nl = b.rfind(b"\n")
        if last_nl > 0:
            b = b[:last_nl]
    return b

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target formats:
# - filename suffix for CZNC::BackupConfigOnce: prefer safe filesystem-friendly strings, non-empty
# - CTemplate::ExpandFile uses two FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls: a search path and a filename to expand
#   We should sometimes provide realistic relative/absolute paths with separators, extensions,
#   include-style paths, and edge-case components like ., .., tildes, and skin/module-like dirs.
#
# The fuzzer framework will split our returned bytes across FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME
# requests as needed. We therefore pack multiple NUL-terminated strings in sequence to seed
# successive FUZZ_PARAM_STR() calls. Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_.,+@#%="
PATH_SEPS = ["/", "\\"]

def _rand_safe_suffix(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Common, valid backup suffixes
    common = [
        ".bak", ".backup", ".old", ".orig", ".sav", ".tmp", ".1", ".~",
        "-backup", "_bak",
    ]
    # Occasionally generate a timestamp-like or mixed suffix
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        return r.choice(common)
    # Alphanumeric with punctuation, 2..12 chars
    n = r.randint(2, 12)
    return "." + "".join(r.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(n))

def _rand_path_component(r: random.Random) -> str:
    choices = [
        "etc", "usr", "local", "znc", "modules", "skins", "templates",
        "conf", "data", "home", "tmp", "var", "lib", "include", "share",
        "..", ".", "~",
    ]
    # Sometimes random word
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        ln = r.randint(1, 10)
        return "".join(r.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + "-_") for _ in range(ln))
    return r.choice(choices)

def _rand_ext(r: random.Random) -> str:
    return r.choice([".conf", ".tmpl", ".html", ".txt", ".cfg", ".ini", ".znc", ""])  # sometimes no ext

def _rand_filename(r: random.Random) -> str:
    base_choices = [
        "znc.conf", "config", "main", "webadmin", "index", "status",
        "motd", "template", "module", "listeners", "users",
    ]
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        base = r.choice(base_choices)
        # maybe add extension if not present
        if "." not in base and r.random() < 0.7:
            base += _rand_ext(r)
    else:
        ln = r.randint(1, 12)
        base = "".join(r.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_+") for _ in range(ln))
        base += _rand_ext(r)
    return base

def _rand_path(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build absolute or relative path, possibly with include-like prefix
    is_abs = r.random() < 0.5
    sep = r.choice(PATH_SEPS)
    parts: List[str] = []
    # prefix like skins/default or modules/modname
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        head = r.choice(["skins", "modules", "data", "templates", "conf"])  # ZNC-like dirs
        parts.append(head)
        if r.random() < 0.7:
            parts.append(r.choice(["default", "bootstrap", "webadmin", "extra"]))
    # mid components
    for _ in range(r.randint(0, 3)):
        parts.append(_rand_path_component(r))
    # filename at end
    parts.append(_rand_filename(r))
    path = sep.join(parts)
    if is_abs:
        path = sep + path if not path.startswith(sep) else path
    return path

def _rand_bool(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Represented as non-empty string token the harness will parse as unsigned int then %2
    return str(r.randint(0, 3))

def _pack_cstrings(strings: List[str]) -> bytes:
    # Join as NUL-terminated strings; ensure max size
    out = bytearray()
    for s in strings:
        b = s.encode('utf-8', 'ignore')
        out.extend(b)
        out.append(0)
        if len(out) > 4096:
            break
    return bytes(out[:4096])

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # We will prepare a sequence covering both stubs:
    # 1) suffix for BackupConfigOnce (non-empty)
    # 2) path for CTemplate::AppendPath
    # 3) boolean-like flag (as unsigned int string) to decide includesOnly
    # 4) filename for CTemplate::ExpandFile
    # 5) fromInc flag (as unsigned int string)

    suffix = _rand_safe_suffix(r)

    # Mix in some special-case suffixes occasionally to hit different code paths
    if r.random() < 0.2:
        suffix = r.choice([".r1", "~backup", "-2025", ".bak1", ".local"])

    path = _rand_path(r)

    includes_only = _rand_bool(r)
    fname = _rand_path(r) if r.random() < 0.5 else _rand_filename(r)
    from_inc = _rand_bool(r)

    # Occasionally provide empty path (meaning no AppendPath call is skipped by stub)
    if r.random() < 0.2:
        path = ""

    # Ensure suffix not empty (fuzzer bails if empty)
    if not suffix:
        suffix = ".bak"

    return _pack_cstrings([suffix, path, includes_only, fname, from_inc])

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: username (ZNC). Should be valid usernames used by ZNC.
# ZNC usernames are typically ASCII, starting with a letter, then letters/digits/_/-/.
# Many stubs prefer existing/valid, non-empty names; others tolerate arbitrary.
# We will generate a small corpus of interesting, valid usernames and package
# them as a newline-delimited blob so FUZZ_PARAM_STR() pulls from this pool.
# Keep under 4096 bytes.

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + "_-"

STATIC_USERNAMES = [
    # Minimal and boundary cases
    "a",
    "u1",
    "user",
    "user_",
    "user-",
    "user.name",  # include dot to exercise cleaners (some code may clean dots)
    "UserName",   # mixed case
    "user123",
    "znc",
    "admin",
    # Longer cases near typical limits (choose 32/63-ish)
    "u" * 15,
    "user_" + "x" * 20,
    "alpha_beta-gamma",
    "client1-networkA",  # resembles user/network style inputs
    # With separators some paths may parse (identifier, network, client)
    "user/network",
    "user@client",
    "user/network@client",
]

def rand_username(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Ensure starts with a letter to be likely valid in ZNC
    length = rng.randint(1, 24)
    start = rng.choice(string.ascii_letters)
    if length == 1:
        return start
    rest = ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(length - 1))
    # Occasionally embed separators to exercise parsers in stubs using ParseUser / identifiers
    if rng.random() < 0.2 and length > 4:
        insert_pos = rng.randint(1, len(rest) - 1)
        sep = rng.choice(['/','@','.'])
        rest = rest[:insert_pos] + sep + rest[insert_pos:]
    return start + rest

def build_corpus(seed: int) -> List[str]:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    corpus = list(STATIC_USERNAMES)
    # Add random valid usernames
    for _ in range(40):
        corpus.append(rand_username(rng))
    # De-duplicate while preserving order
    seen = set()
    uniq = []
    for u in corpus:
        if u not in seen and u:
            seen.add(u)
            uniq.append(u)
    # Ensure at least a couple of very simple names first
    front = ["u", "test", "fuzzuser"]
    for f in reversed(front):
        if f in uniq:
            uniq.remove(f)
        uniq.insert(0, f)
    return uniq

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    users = build_corpus(seed)
    # Shuffle lightly but keep first few simple ones at front
    head = users[:3]
    tail = users[3:]
    rng.shuffle(tail)
    ordered = head + tail
    # Join into newline-delimited payload; FUZZ_PARAM_STR() will consume slices
    blob = "\n".join(ordered)
    # Ensure size bound
    b = blob.encode('utf-8')
    if len(b) > 4096:
        # Truncate on line boundaries
        lines = ordered
        out = []
        size = 0
        for line in lines:
            enc = (line + "\n").encode('utf-8')
            if size + len(enc) > 4096:
                break
            out.append(enc)
            size += len(enc)
        b = b"".join(out)
    return b

import random
import string

# Data type: password (opaque string). However, we want to produce bytes that
# are useful initial seeds for the listed fuzz stubs which consume FUZZ_PARAM_STR
# for many authentication-related fields (usernames, passwords, SASL payloads,
# server hostnames, etc.). FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME is not used in these stubs.
#
# Strategy:
# - Build a small corpus of interesting ASCII and binary password-like strings,
#   including typical, edge-case, and high-entropy variants.
# - Serialize one or more strings separated by NUL ("\x00") so the harness can
#   split them into multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls deterministically if it uses a
#   stream source. Many fuzzers use a single buffer as a random source.
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.
# - Use the seed to choose a mixture of: short/empty, long, unicode, base64-ish,
#   URL-like, IRC-ish nick, hostnames, salts, and high-entropy bytes.
#
# The stubs expect multiple independent strings for:
#  - usernames, passwords (CClientAuth, AuthUser, Web OnLogin)
#  - PASS/NICK/IDENT/REALNAME (OnIRCRegistration)
#  - SASL user/pass/authz (StartSASLPasswordCheck)
#  - server host/pass (AddServer/DelServer/CServer ctor)
# Therefore we output a sequence of 32+ strings to cover these consumers.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

ASCII = string.ascii_letters + string.digits
PRINTABLE_SAFE = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " "


def rand_ascii(rng, n):
    return ''.join(rng.choice(ASCII) for _ in range(n))


def rand_printable(rng, n):
    return ''.join(rng.choice(PRINTABLE_SAFE) for _ in range(n))


def rand_unicode(rng, n):
    # Mix of BMP and some emoji range code points
    out = []
    for _ in range(n):
        t = rng.random()
        if t < 0.6:
            out.append(chr(rng.randint(0x20, 0x7E)))
        elif t < 0.85:
            out.append(chr(rng.randint(0x00A1, 0x07FF)))
        elif t < 0.97:
            out.append(chr(rng.randint(0x0800, 0xD7FF)))
        else:
            # Emojis (a rough slice)
            out.append(chr(rng.randint(0x1F300, 0x1F6FF)))
    return ''.join(out)


def rand_bytes(rng, n):
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def make_hostname(rng):
    labels = []
    num = rng.randint(2, 4)
    for i in range(num):
        L = rng.randint(1, 10)
        s = rand_ascii(rng, L).lower()
        labels.append(s)
    return '.'.join(labels)


def make_irc_nick(rng):
    # RFC 2812-ish: start with letter or special, keep simple here
    start = rng.choice(string.ascii_letters)
    rest_len = rng.randint(0, 15)
    rest_chars = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-[]\\`^{}_"
    rest = ''.join(rng.choice(rest_chars) for _ in range(rest_len))
    return start + rest


def make_passwords_corpus(rng):
    corpus = []
    # Typical simple
    corpus += [
        "password", "123456", "letmein", "admin", "root", "znc",
        "pass", "userpass", "P@ssw0rd!", "toor",
    ]
    # Empty and whitespace variations
    corpus += ["", " ", "\t", "\n", "\r\n"]
    # Long ASCII
    corpus.append(rand_ascii(rng, 128))
    corpus.append(rand_printable(rng, 256))
    # Unicode
    corpus += [rand_unicode(rng, 16), rand_unicode(rng, 64)]
    # High-entropy bytes hex/base64-like
    b = rand_bytes(rng, 32)
    corpus.append(b.hex())
    # URL-like
    corpus += [
        "http://" + make_hostname(rng) + "/", 
        "https://" + make_hostname(rng) + "/api?x=1&y=2",
    ]
    # IRC-related
    corpus += [make_irc_nick(rng), "#channel", "&local", "+mode", "-modestr"]
    # Salts
    corpus += [rand_ascii(rng, 8), rand_ascii(rng, 12)]
    # SASL authzid-like (user/network/client syntax common in ZNC)
    user = make_irc_nick(rng)
    net = rand_ascii(rng, rng.randint(3, 8)).lower()
    ident = rand_ascii(rng, rng.randint(3, 6)).lower()
    corpus += [f"{user}/{net}:{ident}"]
    return corpus


def assemble_strings(rng):
    parts = []
    # Ensure we provide enough values for many FUZZ_PARAM_STR uses
    base = make_passwords_corpus(rng)
    # Hostnames and server strings
    for _ in range(5):
        host = make_hostname(rng)
        port = rng.randint(1, 65535)
        pw = rand_ascii(rng, rng.randint(0, 16))
        server_str = f"{host}:{port}:{pw}"
        parts.append(host)
        parts.append(server_str)
    # User/Pass pairs
    for _ in range(6):
        u = make_irc_nick(rng)
        p = rand_printable(rng, rng.randint(0, 24))
        parts.append(u)
        parts.append(p)
    # PASS/NICK/IDENT/REALNAME sets
    for _ in range(3):
        parts.append(rand_printable(rng, rng.randint(0, 16)))  # PASS
        parts.append(make_irc_nick(rng))  # NICK
        parts.append(rand_ascii(rng, rng.randint(3, 10)))  # IDENT
        parts.append(rand_unicode(rng, rng.randint(3, 16)))  # REALNAME
    # SASL triplets
    for _ in range(4):
        parts.append(make_irc_nick(rng))
        parts.append(rand_printable(rng, rng.randint(0, 32)))
        parts.append(rand_printable(rng, rng.randint(0, 32)))
    # Web login repeated
    for _ in range(4):
        parts.append(rand_ascii(rng, rng.randint(3, 10)))
        parts.append(rand_printable(rng, rng.randint(3, 20)))
    # Add the base corpus at the end
    parts.extend(base)
    # Ensure some very short and very long entries
    parts.append("")
    parts.append(rand_printable(rng, 300))
    return parts


def serialize(parts):
    # Join with NUL separators to allow easy tokenization by consumers.
    out = bytearray()
    sep = b"\x00"
    for s in parts:
        if isinstance(s, bytes):
            chunk = s
        else:
            chunk = s.encode('utf-8', errors='surrogatepass')
        # Avoid exceeding MAX_TOTAL; if next chunk would overflow, stop.
        need = len(chunk) + (0 if not out else 1)
        if len(out) + need > MAX_TOTAL:
            break
        if out:
            out += sep
        out += chunk
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    parts = assemble_strings(rng)
    rng.shuffle(parts)
    return serialize(parts)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: identifier string
# Used as: skin names, status prefixes, page names, encoding names, listener names, etc.
# Goals:
#  - Produce short, human-readable ASCII identifiers that round-trip in CString
#  - Cover interesting categories likely to trigger different code paths
#  - Keep size <= 4096 bytes (we produce small strings)
#  - Deterministic with seed, but varied per call

SAFE_ALPHA = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_"
CHANNEL_PREFIXES = ["#", "&"]
ENCODINGS = [
    "UTF-8", "utf8", "ISO-8859-1", "ISO-2022-JP", "Shift_JIS", "Windows-1251",
    "KOI8-R", "GB18030", "EUC-KR", "Big5", "US-ASCII"
]
LANGS = ["en", "de", "fr", "es", "ru", "ja", "zh_CN", "pt_BR", "it", "nl"]
SKINS = ["default", "dark", "light", "classic", "modern"]
URI_PREFIXES = ["/", "/znc", "/admin", "/api", "/skin"]
CAP_KEYS = ["sasl", "batch", "server-time", "account-notify", "message-tags"]
ISUPPORT_KEYS = ["NETWORK", "PREFIX", "CHANTYPES", "CHANMODES", "NICKLEN", "CASEMAPPING"]
IDENT_START = string.ascii_letters
IDENT_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_"


def _rand_ident(rng: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=24) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_ALPHA) for _ in range(n))


def _rand_channel(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    base = _rand_ident(rng, 1, 16)
    return rng.choice(CHANNEL_PREFIXES) + base


def _rand_encoding(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        return rng.choice(ENCODINGS)
    # random but plausible token with dashes/underscores
    parts = [_rand_ident(rng, 2, 6) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3))]
    return "-".join(parts)


def _rand_lang(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        return rng.choice(LANGS)
    return _rand_ident(rng, 2, 8)


def _rand_uri_prefix(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        return rng.choice(URI_PREFIXES)
    return "/" + _rand_ident(rng, 1, 10)


def _rand_ident_strict(rng: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=16) -> str:
    # ident-like (for SetIdent, usernames)
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    s = rng.choice(IDENT_START)
    s += ''.join(rng.choice(IDENT_CHARS) for _ in range(n - 1))
    return s


def _cases(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Curate a set of interesting identifiers mapping to fuzzer stub usage
    L: List[str] = []
    # Empty and special default triggers
    L.append("")                  # For SetStatusPrefix to coerce to "*"
    L.append("*")                 # Explicit default prefix
    # Skins
    L.extend(SKINS)
    # Encodings
    L.extend(ENCODINGS[:])
    # Languages
    L.extend(LANGS[:])
    # URI prefixes and page names
    L.extend([_rand_uri_prefix(rng) for _ in range(3)])
    L.extend(["page", "tmpl", "status", "help", "index"])    
    # Channel-like strings
    L.extend([_rand_channel(rng) for _ in range(3)])
    # Identifiers/user-like
    L.extend([_rand_ident_strict(rng) for _ in range(3)])
    # Capability and ISUPPORT keys
    L.extend(CAP_KEYS)
    L.extend(ISUPPORT_KEYS)
    # Listener names
    L.extend(["znc_fuzz_listener", "znc_fuzz_listenall", "znc_fuzz_connect"])    
    # Random safe identifiers of varying lengths
    L.extend([_rand_ident(rng, 1, 8), _rand_ident(rng, 5, 12), _rand_ident(rng, 10, 20)])
    # Mixed tokens that could be filenames (for UNIX paths are provided by FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME separately)
    L.extend(["mod", "admin", "user", "network", "query", "chan"])    
    # Encoding-ish and language-ish randoms
    L.append(_rand_encoding(rng))
    L.append(_rand_lang(rng))
    return L


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    candidates = _cases(rng)
    # Weight selection towards non-empty but still occasionally choose empty
    weights = []
    for s in candidates:
        if s == "":
            weights.append(1)
        else:
            # Prefer moderate sized tokens
            w = 3
            if len(s) <= 3:
                w = 2
            elif len(s) >= 12:
                w = 4
            weights.append(w)
    # Choose 1 main token; occasionally prefix with "/" when it looks like a page
    chosen = rng.choices(candidates, weights=weights, k=1)[0]
    # Ensure maximal length constraint; most stubs expect small strings
    chosen = chosen[:64]
    # Return as UTF-8 bytes
    out = chosen.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    if len(out) > 4096:
        out = out[:4096]
    return out

import random
from typing import List

# Generator for OpenSSL cipher list strings suitable for CZNC::SetSSLCiphers
# It returns bytes so the fuzzing harness can feed FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME.
# We focus on producing valid and interesting cipher-list expressions per OpenSSL syntax.
# Size is limited to <=4096 bytes.

CIPHER_TOKENS = [
    # Cipher group aliases
    "DEFAULT", "ALL", "HIGH", "MEDIUM", "LOW", "FIPS", "SUITEB128", "SUITEB192",
    "AES", "AESGCM", "AESCCM", "CHACHA20", "3DES", "SHA", "SHA1", "SHA256", "SHA384",
    "RSA", "ECDHE", "DHE", "PSK", "KRB5", "SRP", "aNULL", "eNULL", "kRSA", "kECDHE",
    "kEECDH", "kEDH", "kDHE", "kPSK", "kSRP", "aRSA", "aECDSA", "aPSK",
    # Protocol/version selectors (for legacy OpenSSL cipher string language)
    "TLSv1", "TLSv1.2", "TLSv1.3",
]

# Individual named ciphers (legacy and common names). Names are included for variety; OpenSSL will ignore unknowns safely.
NAMED_CIPHERS = [
    "ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384",
    "ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384",
    "ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256",
    "ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256",
    "DHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384",
    "DHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256",
    "AES256-GCM-SHA384",
    "AES128-GCM-SHA256",
    "ECDHE-RSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305",
    "ECDHE-ECDSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305",
    "TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384",
    "TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256",
    "TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256",
    "ECDHE-RSA-AES256-SHA384",
    "ECDHE-RSA-AES128-SHA256",
    "AES256-SHA",
    "AES128-SHA",
    "DES-CBC3-SHA",
]

# Modifiers per OpenSSL cipher list language
MODIFIERS = [
    "!",   # exclude
    "+",   # move to end (lower priority)
    "-",   # remove from list
    "@STRENGTH",  # sort by strength (used as a standalone selector)
]

# TLS1.3 ciphers are not filtered by cipher string in some OpenSSL versions unless using @SECLEVEL etc.,
# but including them is still valid/interesting.

def _rand_bool(r: random.Random, p: float) -> bool:
    return r.random() < p

def _one_element(r: random.Random) -> str:
    choice_pool: List[str] = []
    # Mix groups and named ciphers
    choice_pool.extend(CIPHER_TOKENS)
    choice_pool.extend(NAMED_CIPHERS)
    elem = r.choice(choice_pool)
    # Optionally prefix with a modifier (exclude/remove/priority)
    if elem != "@STRENGTH" and _rand_bool(r, 0.5):
        mod = r.choice(["!", "+", "-"])
        elem = mod + elem
    return elem

def _build_cipher_string(r: random.Random) -> str:
    parts: List[str] = []

    # Start with a sensible base occasionally
    bases = [
        "DEFAULT",
        "HIGH:!aNULL:!eNULL:!MD5:!RC4",
        "HIGH:@STRENGTH",
        "ALL:!aNULL:!eNULL",
        "DEFAULT:@STRENGTH",
        "TLSv1.2:!aNULL:!eNULL",
    ]
    if _rand_bool(r, 0.7):
        parts.append(r.choice(bases))

    # Add several random elements separated by ':'
    n_extra = r.randint(2, 12)
    for _ in range(n_extra):
        if _rand_bool(r, 0.15):
            parts.append("@STRENGTH")
            continue
        parts.append(_one_element(r))

    # Occasionally add a block emphasizing/negating specific families
    if _rand_bool(r, 0.6):
        tail_blocks = [
            "!aNULL:!eNULL:!SSLv2:!SSLv3",
            "+CHACHA20:!RC4",
            "!PSK:!SRP",
            "kECDHE:+aECDSA",
            "EECDH:!EDH",
        ]
        parts.append(r.choice(tail_blocks))

    # Shuffle subparts sometimes to vary priority
    if _rand_bool(r, 0.4):
        r.shuffle(parts)

    # Join with ':' but ensure no accidental empty segments
    cipher_str = ":".join([p for p in parts if p])

    # Truncate to reasonable size (OpenSSL accepts long strings, but keep < 1024)
    return cipher_str[:1024]

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # With some probability generate multiple alternative cipher strings separated by newlines;
    # FUZZ_PARAM_STR typically reads one string, but if used for files FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME,
    # multiple lines provide more coverage while remaining valid lines individually.
    lines: List[str] = []
    num_lines = 1 if _rand_bool(r, 0.7) else r.randint(2, 6)

    # Include a few curated valid presets to exercise known branches
    presets = [
        "HIGH:!aNULL:@STRENGTH",
        "DEFAULT",
        "TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384:TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256:TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256",
        "ALL:!aNULL:!eNULL:!MD5:!RC4",
    ]

    for i in range(num_lines):
        if _rand_bool(r, 0.35):
            line = r.choice(presets)
        else:
            line = _build_cipher_string(r)
        # Randomly surround with optional whitespace (OpenSSL usually tolerates spaces)
        if _rand_bool(r, 0.3):
            ws_left = "" if _rand_bool(r, 0.5) else " " * r.randint(1, 3)
            ws_right = "" if _rand_bool(r, 0.5) else " " * r.randint(1, 3)
            line = f"{ws_left}{line}{ws_right}"
        lines.append(line)

    data = ("\n".join(lines)).encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
    # Ensure limit
    return data[:4096]

import random
from typing import List

# Data type: SSL/TLS protocol list string for ZNC::SetSSLProtocols
# We generate plausible protocol selection strings that ZNC might accept.
# Covering: single versions, plus-separated combinations, keywords, and edge cases
# while remaining valid-looking (not random garbage), to exercise different paths.

_SINGLE_TOKENS: List[str] = [
    # Common protocol tokens across OpenSSL/LibreSSL
    "TLSv1",
    "TLSv1.0",
    "TLSv1.1",
    "TLSv1.2",
    "TLSv1.3",
    # Sometimes seen aliases
    "TLS1",
    "TLS1.0",
    "TLS1.1",
    "TLS1.2",
    "TLS1.3",
]

# Some composite presets occasionally supported by apps/libraries
_COMPOSITES: List[str] = [
    "TLSv1.2+TLSv1.3",
    "TLSv1.1+TLSv1.2",
    "TLSv1+TLSv1.1+TLSv1.2",
    "TLS1.2+TLS1.3",
]

# Feature/keyword-style options that some builds recognize
_KEYWORDS: List[str] = [
    "DEFAULT",
    "ALL",
    "SECURE",
    "MODERN",
    "INTERMEDIATE",
]

# Delimiters that might be accepted (primarily '+', but include ',' and ':')
_DELIMS = ['+', ',', ':']


def _rand_subset(rng: random.Random, items: List[str], min_len: int, max_len: int) -> List[str]:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # sample without replacement but allow duplicates via occasional dup pick
    if n <= len(items):
        subset = rng.sample(items, n)
    else:
        subset = items[:] + rng.sample(items, n - len(items))
    # Occasionally shuffle
    rng.shuffle(subset)
    return subset


def _maybe_prefix_suffix(rng: random.Random, s: str) -> str:
    # Sometimes add whitespace which CString::Trim may tolerate
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        left = ' ' * rng.randint(0, 2)
        right = ' ' * rng.randint(0, 2)
        s = f"{left}{s}{right}"
    return s


def _build_proto_string(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.20:
        # Single token
        s = rng.choice(_SINGLE_TOKENS)
    elif choice < 0.40:
        # Composite from predefined list
        s = rng.choice(_COMPOSITES)
    elif choice < 0.55:
        # Keyword by itself
        s = rng.choice(_KEYWORDS)
    elif choice < 0.80:
        # Constructed composite of 2-4 single tokens with a random delimiter
        parts = _rand_subset(rng, _SINGLE_TOKENS, 2, 4)
        delim = rng.choice(_DELIMS)
        s = delim.join(parts)
    else:
        # Mixed: maybe a keyword + tokens
        parts = []
        if rng.random() < 0.7:
            parts.append(rng.choice(_KEYWORDS))
        parts.extend(_rand_subset(rng, _SINGLE_TOKENS, 1, 3))
        delim = rng.choice(_DELIMS)
        s = delim.join(parts)
    return _maybe_prefix_suffix(rng, s)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Create multiple candidates and pick one to keep results varying while seeded
    candidates = []
    count = rng.randint(1, 5)
    for _ in range(count):
        candidates.append(_build_proto_string(rng))
    # Prefer a candidate with TLSv1.3 sometimes to exercise modern stacks
    prefer = [c for c in candidates if "1.3" in c or "v1.3" in c]
    s = rng.choice(prefer if prefer and rng.random() < 0.6 else candidates)
    data = s.encode('utf-8')
    # Ensure we stay under 4096 bytes
    return data[:4096]

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for CTCP payloads (without surrounding \x01)
# Target fuzzers use:
# - CClient::StatusCTCP: expects a single command-like token, possibly with args
# - CUser::AddCTCPReply: verb (CTCP command) and reply text
# - CCTCPMessage/CActionMessage builders: SetText expects CTCP inner text
#
# We therefore produce a single bytes buffer which will be used by FUZZ_PARAM_STR()
# and aims to be a valid/interesting CTCP inner text, including popular verbs
# and varying arguments. Size kept <= 4096.

CTCP_VERBS = [
    "ACTION", "VERSION", "PING", "TIME", "CLIENTINFO", "SOURCE", "FINGER",
    "USERINFO", "ERRMSG", "SOUND", "AVATAR", "DCC", "SED", "UPTIME",
]

ACTIONS = [
    "waves", "smiles", "shrugs", "joins the channel", "is testing ZNC",
    "drinks coffee", "rolls 1d20", "facepalms", "high-fives everyone",
]

USER_AGENTS = [
    "ZNC 1.9.0", "weechat 4.2", "irssi 1.4", "HexChat 2.16", "mIRC 7.77",
    "KiwiIRC", "LimeChat", "Colloquy", "Textual", "ircII",
]

HOSTS = [
    "example.com", "irc.example.net", "znc.local", "localhost", "server.local",
]

CHANNELS = ["#znc", "#general", "#test", "#dev", "#random"]
NICKS = ["alice", "bob", "charlie", "dave", "eve", "mallory"]
FILES = ["readme.txt", "image.png", "file.bin", "report.pdf", "music.mp3"]

PRINTABLE_SAFE = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " .,:;_-+/@#[](){}<>|~?=\"'"


def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, arr: List[str]) -> str:
    return rng.choice(arr)


def _random_words(rng: random.Random, k: int) -> str:
    words = []
    for _ in range(k):
        ln = rng.randint(1, 10)
        s = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase) for _ in range(ln))
        words.append(s)
    return ' '.join(words)


def _random_safe_text(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 0, max_len: int = 64) -> str:
    L = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(rng.choice(PRINTABLE_SAFE) for _ in range(L)).strip()


def _build_action(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # ACTION verb requires an argument describing the action
    act = _rand_choice(rng, ACTIONS)
    extra = ''
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        extra = ' ' + _random_words(rng, rng.randint(1, 4))
    return f"ACTION {act}{extra}".strip()


def _build_version(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    ua = _rand_choice(rng, USER_AGENTS)
    plat = rng.choice(["Windows", "Linux", "macOS", "FreeBSD", "OpenBSD", "NetBSD"]) if rng.random() < 0.7 else _random_safe_text(rng, 3, 12)
    return f"VERSION {ua} ({plat})"


def _build_ping(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # PING with a numeric or timestamp-like token
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        token = str(rng.randrange(10**9, 10**10))
    else:
        token = str(rng.randrange(0, 99999999))
    return f"PING {token}"


def _build_time(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    tz = rng.choice(["UTC", "PST", "EST", "CET", "EET", "IST", "JST", "AEDT"]) if rng.random() < 0.6 else _random_safe_text(rng, 2, 6)
    return f"TIME {tz}"


def _build_clientinfo(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # CLIENTINFO optionally followed by a verb or list
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        sub = _rand_choice(rng, CTCP_VERBS)
    else:
        sub = ' '.join(rng.sample(CTCP_VERBS, rng.randint(1, min(4, len(CTCP_VERBS)))))
    return f"CLIENTINFO {sub}"


def _build_finger(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    who = rng.choice(NICKS) if rng.random() < 0.7 else _random_safe_text(rng, 3, 10)
    return f"FINGER {who}@{_rand_choice(rng, HOSTS)}"


def _build_userinfo(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    txt = _random_safe_text(rng, 8, 64)
    return f"USERINFO {txt}"


def _build_errmsg(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    code = rng.choice(["401", "402", "404", "500"]) if rng.random() < 0.5 else str(rng.randrange(100, 599))
    msg = _random_safe_text(rng, 4, 40)
    return f"ERRMSG {code} {msg}"


def _build_sound(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    snd = rng.choice(["beep.wav", "ding.avi", "notify.mp3", "pop.ogg", "alert.aiff"]) if rng.random() < 0.7 else _random_safe_text(rng, 3, 12)
    target = rng.choice(NICKS + CHANNELS) if rng.random() < 0.5 else ''
    return (f"SOUND {snd} {target}" if target else f"SOUND {snd}").strip()


def _build_avatar(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Some clients use AVATAR request/reply
    sub = rng.choice(["REQUEST", "REPLY"]) if rng.random() < 0.7 else _random_safe_text(rng, 3, 8)
    val = rng.choice(FILES)
    return f"AVATAR {sub} {val}"


def _build_dcc(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # DCC with plausible subcommands without triggering actual transfers
    sub = rng.choice(["CHAT", "RESUME", "SEND", "ACCEPT", "TSEND"])
    name = rng.choice(FILES) if sub != "CHAT" else _rand_choice(rng, NICKS)
    # Use safe placeholders for IP/port/size
    ip = str(rng.randrange(1, 2**32))
    port = str(rng.randrange(1024, 65535))
    size = str(rng.randrange(1, 10_000_000))
    if sub in ("SEND", "TSEND"):
        return f"DCC {sub} {name} {ip} {port} {size}"
    elif sub == "RESUME":
        return f"DCC RESUME {name} {port} {size}"
    elif sub == "ACCEPT":
        return f"DCC ACCEPT {name} {port} {size}"
    else:  # CHAT
        return f"DCC CHAT chat {ip} {port}"


def _build_generic(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    verb = rng.choice(CTCP_VERBS + ["FOO", "BAR", "ECHO", "X-TEST", "LONGVERB"])
    args = []
    # 0-4 args
    for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 4)):
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            args.append(_random_words(rng, rng.randint(1, 3)))
        else:
            args.append(_random_safe_text(rng, 1, 12))
    return ' '.join([verb] + args).strip()


BUILDERS = [
    _build_action,
    _build_version,
    _build_ping,
    _build_time,
    _build_clientinfo,
    _build_finger,
    _build_userinfo,
    _build_errmsg,
    _build_sound,
    _build_avatar,
    _build_dcc,
    _build_generic,
]


def _maybe_truncate(s: str, maxlen: int, rng: random.Random) -> str:
    if len(s) <= maxlen:
        return s
    # Prefer cutting at whitespace to keep tokens intact
    cut = rng.randrange(max(16, maxlen - 64), maxlen)
    # Find last space before cut
    sp = s.rfind(' ', 0, cut)
    if sp >= 0 and sp >= maxlen - 64:
        return s[:sp]
    return s[:maxlen]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose one or compose multiple for richer payloads used by StatusCTCP
    count = 1 if rng.random() < 0.7 else rng.randint(2, 3)
    parts = []
    for _ in range(count):
        b = rng.choice(BUILDERS)
        parts.append(b(rng))

    payload = ' | '.join(parts) if count > 1 else parts[0]

    # Ensure max size reasonable for IRC (<= 512 in fuzzer truncates)
    payload = _maybe_truncate(payload, 480, rng)

    # Guarantee non-empty and ASCII-friendly
    if not payload.strip():
        payload = "VERSION ZNC"

    # Return as raw bytes; CTCP framing will be applied by callers where needed
    data = payload.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    # Respect global limit (<= 4096)
    return data[:4096]

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets inputs consumed by FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME in
# fuzzer stubs exercising IRC capability handling (CAP). It should yield valid,
# interesting IRCv3 capability names and related values.
#
# Target stubs expect strings for capability names (cap) and sometimes values.
# Valid caps are typically lowercase tokens with hyphens, optionally vendor
# prefixes with a slash, e.g. "server-time", "message-tags", "draft/label".
# Lengths are constrained in the stubs (commonly <= 64 for caps, <= 256 for
# values). We produce a small corpus per call, concatenated, so the harness can
# split them to feed multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR invocations.

# A compact dictionary of well-known IRCv3 capabilities and realistic values.
BASE_CAPS = [
    "server-time",
    "message-tags",
    "batch",
    "account-notify",
    "away-notify",
    "invite-notify",
    "extended-join",
    "chghost",
    "sasl",
    "echo-message",
    "labeled-response",
    "draft/labeled-response",
    "draft/message-tags-0.2",
    "znc.in/server-time-iso",
    "cap-notify",
    "multi-prefix",
    "userhost-in-names",
]

# Some vendor/experimental prefixed caps
VENDOR_PREFIXES = [
    "draft/",
    "vendor/",
    "znc.in/",
    "soju.im/",
    "chathistory/",
]

# Possible LS values for some caps (e.g., sasl=PLAIN,EXTERNAL or server-time)
CAP_LS_KV = [
    ("sasl", ["PLAIN", "EXTERNAL", "PLAIN,EXTERNAL", "SCRAM-SHA-256"]),
    ("message-tags", ["1"]),
    ("batch", ["1"]),
    ("labeled-response", ["1"]),
    ("draft/labeled-response", ["1"]),
    ("server-time", ["1", "v=3.2"]),
]

# Additional arbitrary but valid-looking values to exercise value paths
EXTRA_VALUES = [
    "1",
    "true",
    "false",
    "yes",
    "no",
    "enabled",
    "disabled",
    "v=3.2",
]


def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, arr: List[str]) -> str:
    return arr[rng.randrange(0, len(arr))]


def _rand_token(rng: random.Random, alphabet: str, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return "".join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))


def _random_cap(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # 60% choose from known, 40% synthesize a valid token (lowercase, hyphens, optional vendor prefix)
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        cap = _rand_choice(rng, BASE_CAPS)
    else:
        base = _rand_token(rng, string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits, 3, 12)
        # Optionally insert hyphens
        if rng.random() < 0.7:
            parts = [base]
            for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 2)):
                parts.append(_rand_token(rng, string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits, 2, 8))
            base = "-".join(parts)
        # Optional vendor prefix
        if rng.random() < 0.4:
            cap = _rand_choice(rng, VENDOR_PREFIXES) + base
        else:
            cap = base
    # Enforce max length used by stubs (<=64)
    return cap[:64]


def _random_value_for_cap(rng: random.Random, cap: str) -> str:
    for k, vals in CAP_LS_KV:
        if cap == k:
            return _rand_choice(rng, vals)
    # Try prefix match for draft/ variants
    if cap.startswith("draft/labeled-response"):
        return "1"
    if cap.startswith("server-time"):
        return _rand_choice(rng, ["1", "v=3.2"])
    # Otherwise pick an extra value or a small integer
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        return _rand_choice(rng, EXTRA_VALUES)
    return str(rng.randint(0, 9))


def _build_corpus(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    corpus: List[str] = []
    # Include a baseline set of commonly referenced caps in the stubs
    baseline = ["server-time", "sasl", "message-tags"]
    corpus.extend(baseline)
    # Add some accepted-like and unaccepted-like tokens
    for _ in range(rng.randint(4, 8)):
        corpus.append(_random_cap(rng))
    # Add vendor-prefixed examples explicitly
    corpus.extend([
        "draft/label",
        "znc.in/server-time-iso",
        "draft/message-tags-0.2",
    ])
    # Add a couple of values that stubs may pass (NotifyServerDependentCap uses val)
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 6)):
        c = _random_cap(rng)
        v = _random_value_for_cap(rng, c)
        corpus.append(v[:256])
    # Ensure a few unlikely keys to trigger default-return paths
    corpus.extend([
        "znc/fuzz/unknown_" + str(rng.getrandbits(16)),
        "fuzz/" + _random_cap(rng) + "/cap",
    ])
    # Add some duplicates to exercise set and lookup logic paths
    corpus.extend(["server-time", "sasl", "message-tags"])
    return corpus


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    corpus = _build_corpus(rng)
    # Join with newlines so the harness can split into multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR values
    data = "\n".join(corpus)
    # Cap total size to 4 KiB as requested
    return data[:4096].encode("utf-8")

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: IRC message tag name (without value)
# Constraints/guidelines (IRCV3 message tags):
# - Typically lowercase ASCII letters, digits, and special characters: '-', '/', '.' and vendor prefix '+' allowed.
# - Common tags: time, batch, label, msgid, account, typing, reply, draft/*, znc/*, vendor/foo
# - Lengths in fuzzers are capped (64 for client, 128 for server). We'll keep <= 64 to be safe for all.
# - Empty not allowed in some stubs; produce non-empty.
# - Interesting cases: with vendor prefix '+', with slash-separated namespaces, with dots, with dashes, mixed lengths.

MAX_LEN = 64

COMMON_TAGS: List[str] = [
    "time",
    "batch",
    "label",
    "+draft/label",
    "+draft/reply",
    "+draft/typing",
    "msgid",
    "account",
    "server-time",
    "znc.in/playback",
    "znc.in/self-message",
    "account-tag",
    "sts",
    "solanum.chat/oper",
    "typing",
    "reply",
    "echo-message",
    "bot",
]

VENDORS = [
    "+draft", "znc.in", "example.com", "vendor", "solanum.chat", "ircv3.net"
]

PARTS = list(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits)
SEP_BASIC = ["-", "."]
SEP_NS = ["/"]


def rand_tag(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # With some probability, return a known-good common tag
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        t = r.choice(COMMON_TAGS)
    else:
        # Build a vendor-style namespaced tag
        vendor = r.choice(VENDORS)
        # Optional leading '+' for vendor/draft tags
        lead_plus = "+" if r.random() < 0.5 else ""
        # Build 1-3 path segments
        seg_count = r.randint(1, 3)
        segs = []
        for _ in range(seg_count):
            # segment with letters/digits and occasionally dash/dot inside
            length = r.randint(3, 12)
            s = []
            for i in range(length):
                if i > 0 and r.random() < 0.15:
                    s.append(r.choice(SEP_BASIC))
                else:
                    s.append(r.choice(PARTS))
            segs.append("".join(s))
        t = f"{lead_plus}{vendor}/" + "/".join(segs)
    # Ensure lowercase and trim to MAX_LEN
    t = t.lower()
    if not t:
        t = "time"
    if len(t) > MAX_LEN:
        t = t[:MAX_LEN]
    return t


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Generate a small corpus of tags in one buffer, separated by newlines,
    # so different FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls can read different slices of the same buffer.
    count = r.randint(1, 8)
    tags = []
    for _ in range(count):
        tags.append(rand_tag(r))
    payload = "\n".join(tags)
    # Guarantee at least one even-length tag (for CIRCSock stub that uses len%2)
    if all(len(t) % 2 == 1 for t in tags):
        # Adjust by appending an 'a' to first tag to make even
        tags[0] = (tags[0] + "a")[:MAX_LEN]
        payload = "\n".join(tags)
    # Ensure non-empty and within 4096 bytes
    payload_bytes = payload.encode("utf-8")
    if not payload_bytes:
        payload_bytes = b"time"
    return payload_bytes

import random
import string

# Data type: IRC nickname
# Constraints (approx):
# - Allowed chars: letters, digits, and -[]`^{}_ and underscore
# - No spaces or control chars
# - Length typically <= 32 (stubs clamp to 32 or 64); we keep <= 32
# - Avoid empty; provide variety

ALLOWED_EXTRA = "-[]`^{}_"
ALLOWED = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_" + ALLOWED_EXTRA

# Some interesting nick patterns to exercise different code paths
INTERESTING = [
    "znc_user",
    "nick",
    "alt",
    "user123",
    "A" * 1,
    "B" * 8,
    "C" * 16,
    "D" * 31,
    "E" * 32,  # max typical
    "foo_bar",
    "foo-bar",
    "[brack]",
    "{curl}_x",
    "`backtick`",
    "OpNick",
    "owner",
    "guest01",
]

def rand_nick(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Choose a base length with bias towards edge lengths
    choices = [1, 2, 3, 8, 12, 16, 24, 31, 32]
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        length = r.choice(choices)
    else:
        length = r.randint(1, 32)
    # Start with a letter to satisfy stricter servers, but occasionally not
    if r.random() < 0.85:
        first = r.choice(string.ascii_letters)
    else:
        first = r.choice(ALLOWED)
    rest_len = max(0, length - 1)
    rest = "".join(r.choice(ALLOWED) for _ in range(rest_len))
    nick = first + rest
    # Occasionally insert one of the canned interesting patterns
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        nick = r.choice(INTERESTING)
    # Ensure not empty and clamp to 32
    return nick[:32] or "znc_user"

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Build multiple nicknames separated by newlines so FUZZ_PARAM_STR can
    # consume from this buffer multiple times as distinct strings.
    # Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.
    n_items = r.randint(3, 12)
    nicks = []
    # Include a couple of deterministic interesting cases up front
    nicks.append("znc_user")
    nicks.append("nick")
    for _ in range(n_items):
        nicks.append(rand_nick(r))
    # Also include some ident/host-like tokens used by stubs
    idents = [
        "ident", "user", "u_" + str(r.randint(10,99)),
        "id" + str(r.randint(100,999)),
    ]
    hosts = [
        "host", "example.com", "irc.example.net", "xn--irc-msa.com",
        "2001db8::1", "localhost"
    ]
    payload_list = nicks + idents + hosts
    # Join with newlines; keep under 4096
    data = "\n".join(payload_list)
    data = data[:4096]
    return data.encode("utf-8")

import random
import base64
from typing import List, Tuple

# This generator focuses on producing valid and interesting IRC SASL-related buffers
# which will feed FUZZ_PARAM_STR in the following stubs:
# - CClient::SendSASLChallenge: expects a chunk that client code will base64 and split
# - CClient::StartSASLPasswordCheck: expects (user, pass, authzid) strings
# - CClient::ParseUser: expects an auth line like "user[/network][@identifier]"
#
# We therefore build one composite payload consisting of three length-prefixed strings
# so that the harness can slice them deterministically:
#   [u16 len1][bytes1] [u16 len2][bytes2] [u16 len3][bytes3]
# and a fourth for the AUTHENTICATE chunk:
#   [u16 len4][chunk]
#
# Each string is constructed to be valid and interesting for ZNC:
# - user: valid username characters with optional /network and @identifier
# - pass: printable, possibly including special chars that commonly appear
# - authz: either empty (same as user) or a distinct authorization identity
# - chunk: mechanism-dependent payloads, focusing on PLAIN (authz\0authc\0pass),
#          plus a few alternative mechanism seeds like "+" (continue) or large but valid splits.
#
# All lengths are capped per stub limits. Total output <= 4096 bytes.

USER_CHARS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789_-"
NET_CHARS = USER_CHARS + ".-"
ID_CHARS = USER_CHARS + ".-"
PASS_CHARS = (
    "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789"
    "!@#$%^&*()-_=+[]{};:'\",.<>/?|`~"
)


def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, s: str, n: int) -> str:
    return "".join(rng.choice(s) for _ in range(n))


def _mk_username(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Ensure it starts with a letter for validity, rest from USER_CHARS
    name = rng.choice("abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ")
    name += _rand_choice(rng, USER_CHARS, rng.randint(2, 10))
    # Optionally append /network and/or @identifier as ZNC supports ParseUser decorations
    parts = []
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        net = _rand_choice(rng, NET_CHARS, rng.randint(3, 10))
        parts.append(f"/{net}")
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        ident = _rand_choice(rng, ID_CHARS, rng.randint(3, 8))
        parts.append(f"@{ident}")
    return name + ("".join(parts))


def _mk_password(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Prefer reasonable length passwords; allow longer occasionally up to 64
    length = rng.choices([8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64], weights=[10, 10, 8, 6, 4, 2, 1])[0]
    return _rand_choice(rng, PASS_CHARS, length)


def _mk_authz(rng: random.Random, user: str) -> str:
    # Sometimes empty (authz==authc by spec), sometimes another id
    roll = rng.random()
    if roll < 0.3:
        return ""  # empty authzid
    if roll < 0.6:
        # same as clean username without /network or @identifier
        # ZNC allows ParseUser to decorate, but authzid is typically bare
        base = user.split("/")[0].split("@")[0]
        return base
    # different authz id
    return _mk_username(rng).split("/")[0].split("@")[0]


def _mk_plain_chunk(rng: random.Random, authz: str, authc: str, passwd: str) -> bytes:
    # SASL PLAIN payload: authzid NUL authcid NUL passwd, to be base64 by caller
    return authz.encode("utf-8") + b"\x00" + authc.encode("utf-8") + b"\x00" + passwd.encode("utf-8")


def _mk_mech_chunk(rng: random.Random, user: str, pw: str, authz: str) -> bytes:
    # Generate several interesting variants for AUTHENTICATE chunk
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.70:
        # Proper PLAIN payload
        payload = _mk_plain_chunk(rng, authz, user.split("/")[0].split("@")[0], pw)
        # Sometimes pre-base64, sometimes already base64-encoded literal
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            return payload  # raw; stub will base64 it
        else:
            return base64.b64encode(payload)  # pre-encoded text still acceptable
    elif choice < 0.80:
        # "=" indicates empty data (end) in some flows; "+" indicates continue
        return b"+"  # server challenge-like token
    elif choice < 0.90:
        # Split-friendly long but valid payload (client will split into 400-byte chunks when sending)
        payload = _mk_plain_chunk(rng, authz, user.split("/")[0].split("@")[0], pw)
        # Repeat to grow, but keep moderate
        reps = rng.randint(2, 5)
        big = (base64.b64encode(payload) + b".") * reps
        return big[:512]
    else:
        # Other mechanism seed (e.g., XOAUTH2-style JSON blob placeholder)
        blob = {
            "aud": _rand_choice(rng, ID_CHARS, rng.randint(6, 12)),
            "iat": rng.randint(1600000000, 2000000000),
            "sub": user.split("/")[0].split("@")[0],
            "scope": "user:email irc:connect",
        }
        js = ("aud={aud}&iat={iat}&sub={sub}&scope={scope}").format(**blob).encode("utf-8")
        return base64.b64encode(js)


def _pack_len_and_bytes(data: bytes) -> bytes:
    # 16-bit little-endian length prefix
    n = len(data)
    if n > 65535:
        n = 65535
        data = data[:n]
    return n.to_bytes(2, "little") + data


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Build username, password, authzid
    user = _mk_username(rng)
    pw = _mk_password(rng)
    authz = _mk_authz(rng, user)

    # Respect stub caps
    if len(user) > 128:
        user = user[:128]
    if len(pw) > 256:
        pw = pw[:256]
    if len(authz) > 256:
        authz = authz[:256]

    # Build AUTHENTICATE chunk
    chunk = _mk_mech_chunk(rng, user, pw, authz)
    # Bound for SendSASLChallenge stub (<=512)
    if len(chunk) > 512:
        chunk = chunk[:512]

    # Also provide a plausible ParseUser auth line variant
    # Examples: "user", "user/network", "user@id", "user/network@id"
    parse_line = user  # already decorated
    if len(parse_line) > 512:
        parse_line = parse_line[:512]

    # Compose as four length-prefixed segments so the harness can split:
    # 1) user, 2) password, 3) authz, 4) authenticate chunk (raw bytes), 5) parse_line
    parts = [
        _pack_len_and_bytes(user.encode("utf-8")),
        _pack_len_and_bytes(pw.encode("utf-8")),
        _pack_len_and_bytes(authz.encode("utf-8")),
        _pack_len_and_bytes(chunk),
        _pack_len_and_bytes(parse_line.encode("utf-8")),
    ]

    out = b"".join(parts)
    # Ensure size cap
    return out[:4096]
